name: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs
sourceNote: This English text was translated fresh from the Greek text of R. H. Charles, *The Greek Versions of the Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs* (Oxford, 1908), which is in the public domain. His English translation (1908, also public domain) was consulted for sense at hard places, and the wording here was written anew from the Greek; because both follow the same Greek, some stock phrases and formulas (such as burial notices) coincide. No modern copyrighted English translation was used. Verse numbers follow the traditional chapters and verses, and each testament is one chapter of this app; the traditional chapter numbers appear as headings inside each testament. Where the Greek has no line for a traditional verse number (for example Judah 15.2 and Joseph 19.3–7), the number is skipped. The divine name is not written out in these texts; “the Lord” (Greek *Kyrios*) is used as in the source, with God, the Most High, and similar titles. **Date and text.** The book is a set of twelve farewell speeches, in which each son of Jacob looks back on his life, warns his children against a particular vice, and tells what will happen to his tribe. The Greek form was fixed by about AD 200, because Origen seems to know it. The oldest Greek manuscripts are medieval, from about the tenth century on. There is also an Armenian version, a Slavonic version made from the Greek, and a Latin translation made by Robert Grosseteste about 1242. Older Jewish material has turned up in Aramaic and Hebrew fragments from Qumran (an Aramaic *Levi* and a Hebrew *Naphtali*) and in the Aramaic *Levi* from the Cairo Geniza; these show that some of the stories and teachings are much older than the Greek book, but they are not copies of it. **The interpolation debate.** The Greek text contains passages that sound Christian, such as the “Lamb of God” in Joseph 19, a crucifixion in Benjamin 9, and a savior “from Judah and Levi” in several testaments. R. H. Charles held that the book was a Jewish work of about 109–107 BC with a small number of Christian additions, which he marked off as later. Since the work of M. de Jonge (1953), and the commentary by H. W. Hollander and de Jonge (1985), many scholars hold instead that the Greek book is a Christian composition of the second century AD built from older Jewish traditions; others, such as H. C. Kee and J. Becker, have argued for different mixes of Jewish and Christian layers. No one can yet fully separate the layers, and this translation does not try. It translates the whole Greek text as it stands and, where a line sounds Christian, says so in a footnote. **Canon status.** The Testaments are not part of the Jewish, Catholic, Protestant, or Orthodox canons. They were copied in some Armenian Bible manuscripts and were read as edifying Christian and Jewish literature. **About the book.** Reuben warns against women and the spirit of fornication, Simeon against envy, and Levi describes his journey through the heavens, his ordination to the priesthood, and the sins of the priests. Judah tells of his wars and his fall with Tamar, and warns against drink and greed. Issachar teaches simplicity; Zebulun, compassion; Dan, the harm of anger and lying; Naphtali, living by the order of creation; Gad, the damage of hatred; Asher, the “two faces” of good and evil; Joseph, self-control against the wife of Potiphar; and Benjamin, the good mind. In most testaments the son confesses a fault, gives his advice, foretells that his descendants will sin, be scattered, and then be saved through Levi and Judah, and asks to be buried at Hebron.

verses.text: A copy of the testament of Reuben:{a} the things he charged his sons with before his death, in the hundred and twenty-fifth year of his life.
Two years after Joseph’s death he fell ill, and his sons and his sons’ sons gathered to visit him.
He said to them, “My little children, I am dying, and I am setting out on the road my fathers took.”

Seeing Judah, Gad and Asher, his brothers, there, he said to them, “Prop me up, brothers, so I can tell my brothers and my children the things I keep hidden in my heart, since from now on I am fading.”
He got up, kissed them, wept, and said, “Listen, my brothers; turn your ears, all of you, to Reuben your father and to what I command you.

Look: today I call the God of heaven as witness against you, so that you do not go the way of youthful ignorance and sexual immorality, the thing I poured myself out in when I defiled my father Jacob’s bed.{b}
I tell you, he struck me with a heavy blow in my loins for seven months, and if Jacob our father had not prayed to the Lord for me, the Lord was minded to make an end of me.
I was thirty years old when I did that evil thing in the Lord’s sight, and for seven months I lay sick almost to death.
Then, by the free choice of my soul, I repented before the Lord for seven years.
Wine and strong drink I did not drink; meat did not enter my mouth; no bread I craved did I taste. I mourned over my sin, for it was great. Nothing like it will ever be done in Israel.”
“Now hear me, children, about what I saw during my repentance concerning the seven spirits of deceit.
Seven spirits are given against humankind from Beliar,{c} and they are the head of the deeds of youthful rashness.
Seven other spirits were given to a person at creation, so that every human work might be done by them.
The first is the spirit of life, with which the human frame is built. The second is the spirit of sight, which gives rise to desire.
The third is the spirit of hearing, which gives rise to teaching. The fourth is the spirit of smell, to which taste is joined for drawing in air and breath.
The fifth is the spirit of speech, which gives rise to knowledge.
The sixth is the spirit of taste, which gives rise to eating food and drink, and by it strength is built up, since strength rests on food.
The seventh is the spirit of seed and intercourse, with which, through love of pleasure, sin comes in as well.
That is why it is the last in creation and the first in youth: it is full of ignorance, and it leads the young man like a blind man into a pit and like a beast over a cliff.”
“On top of all these there is an eighth, the spirit of sleep, with which was created the trance of nature, the image of death.
With these spirits the spirit of deceit mingles.
First, the spirit of sexual immorality, seated in nature and the senses. Second, the spirit of gluttony, in the belly.
Third, the spirit of fighting, in the liver and the gall. Fourth, the spirit of fawning and trickery, so that by fussing over himself a man may seem handsome.
Fifth, the spirit of arrogance, so that he may strut and think big. Sixth, the spirit of lying, in ruin and jealousy, so that he invents stories even to family and household.

Seventh, the spirit of injustice, with which come theft and grasping, so that he may serve his heart’s love of pleasure; for injustice works hand in hand with the other spirits through taking bribes.{d}
On top of all these the spirit of sleep, the eighth spirit, is joined to deceit and illusion.
So every young man is lost, darkening his mind away from the truth, not understanding the law of God and not heeding the warnings of his fathers, just as I suffered in my youth.
And now, children, love the truth, and it will guard you. I am teaching you: listen to Reuben your father.
Do not fix your attention on a woman’s looks, do not be alone with a married woman, and do not busy yourselves with women’s affairs.
If I had not seen Bilhah{e} bathing in a sheltered place, I would not have fallen into that great lawlessness.
My mind took in the woman’s nakedness and would not let me sleep until I had done the abomination.
For while Jacob our father was away with Isaac his father, and we were in Gader,{f} near Ephrath,{g} that is, Bethlehem, Bilhah was drunk and lay asleep, uncovered, in her bedroom.
I went in, saw her nakedness, and did the impious thing; then I left her sleeping and went out.
At once an angel of God revealed my impiety to my father Jacob. He came and mourned over me, and he never touched her again.”

“So do not fix your attention on women’s beauty, and do not brood on what they do. Walk in singleness of heart, in the fear of the Lord, laboring at your work, letting your mind roam among books and among your flocks, until the Lord gives you the wife he wills, so that you do not suffer as I did.
Until our father’s death I did not have the nerve to look Jacob in the face or to speak to any of my brothers, because of the reproaches.
And to this day my conscience grips me over my sin.
Yet my father comforted me, for he had prayed to the Lord for me that the Lord’s anger might pass from me, as the Lord showed me. From then on I kept careful watch, and I did not sin.
So, my children, keep everything I command you, and you will not sin.

Sexual immorality is the ruin of the soul. It separates from God and brings near to idols, because it is what misleads the mind and understanding, and it brings young men down to Hades before their time.
It has destroyed many. Even if a man is old or nobly born, it makes him a disgrace and a laughingstock before Beliar and the children of men.
Because Joseph kept himself from every woman and cleansed his thoughts of all immorality, he found favor with the Lord and with people.
The Egyptian woman did a great deal to him: she called in sorcerers and brought him potions. But the counsel of his soul would not take in evil desire.
So the God of my fathers rescued him from every death, seen and hidden.
If immorality does not overpower your thinking, neither will Beliar overpower you.”
“Women are evil, my children:{h} because they have no authority or strength over a man, they scheme with outward show, how they may draw him to themselves.
And the man a woman cannot overpower by strength she overpowers by deceit.

Indeed the angel of God told me about them and taught me that women are more easily overcome by the spirit of immorality than a man is. In their heart they plot against men; by adornment they first lead their minds astray, by a glance they sow the poison, and then by the act they take them captive.
For a woman cannot force a man.
So flee immorality, my children, and instruct your wives and daughters not to adorn their heads and faces, because every woman who schemes by these means is kept for everlasting punishment.

That is how they bewitched the Watchers{i} before the flood. Those Watchers kept looking at them, came to desire them, conceived the act in their minds, and changed themselves into the shape of men; and when the women lay with their husbands, the Watchers appeared with them.
The women, longing in their minds for these apparitions, bore giants; for the Watchers appeared to them reaching up to heaven.”
“So guard yourselves against immorality. If you want to stay pure in mind, guard your senses from every woman.
And instruct the women not to keep company with men, so that they too may stay pure in mind.
Constant meetings, even if the impious act is never done, are an incurable sickness for them, and for us an everlasting disgrace from Beliar.
For immorality has neither understanding nor piety in it, and every jealousy lives in its desire.
Therefore you will be jealous of the sons of Levi and seek to be raised above them, but you will not be able to.
God will avenge them, and you will die an evil death.
For the Lord gave the rule to Levi, and to Judah, and with them to me, and to Dan and Joseph, to be rulers.{j}

That is why I command you to listen to Levi: he will know the Lord’s law and will make rulings for justice and for sacrifices on behalf of all Israel until the completion of the times of the anointed high priest,{k} of whom the Lord has spoken.
I adjure you by the God of heaven: each of you deal truly with his neighbor.
Draw near to Levi in humility of heart, so that you may receive a blessing from his mouth.
For he will bless Israel and Judah, since it is in him that the Lord has chosen to reign over all the peoples.
Bow down to his offspring, for he will die for us in wars seen and unseen, and he will be among you an eternal king.”{l}
Then Reuben died, having given these commands to his sons.
They placed him in a coffin until they carried him up from Egypt and buried him in Hebron,{m} in the double cave,{n} where his fathers lay.

notes.text: “Reuben” is explained in Gen 29:32 by a wordplay on “Yahweh has seen my affliction”; the name itself looks like “See, a son!” (Hebrew re’u ben). The meaning is uncertain. In the Greek the name is spelled Roubēm, as often in the Septuagint. Verses in this book are numbered straight through each testament; the subheads give the traditional chapter divisions of Charles’s 1908 Greek edition, so “verse 12 here” can be matched with the usual chapter-and-verse reference.
See Gen 35:22; 49:4. “Poured myself out” echoes Gen 49:4, “unstable as water.”
Beliar (Hebrew Belial, “worthlessness”; the derivation is debated) is the usual name for the chief evil power in the Testaments.
The Greek word (dolēpsia, here spelled dololēpsia) is rare; “taking bribes” or “crafty grabbing” are both possible.
Greek Balla, for Hebrew Bilhah, Rachel’s maid and Jacob’s concubine (Gen 30:3–4). The meaning of the name is uncertain; “timid” and “carefree” have both been suggested.
Gader corresponds to “Eder” (Migdal Eder, “tower of the flock”) in Gen 35:21.
Ephrath (“fruitful,” if from the root p-r-h; uncertain) is identified with Bethlehem (“house of bread”) in Gen 35:19.
The harsh generalizations about women in 5:1–5 belong to the outlook of the writer and are translated as they stand.
The Watchers are the fallen angels of Gen 6:1–4 as retold in 1 Enoch 6–16. Here, unusually, the women are blamed.
The Greek is obscure here; some witnesses read differently. The point is that Levi and Judah hold the leading place.

Greek archiereōs christou, “of an anointed high priest” or “of Christ the high priest.” Charles took the line as Jewish, referring to a Hasmonean priest-king; others (e.g., de Jonge) read the whole work as Christian in its present form. See the introduction.
“He will die for us” may be a Christian touch; the referent (“his offspring”) is ambiguous between Levi’s line and Judah’s.
Hebron perhaps means “association” or “league” (from the root h-b-r); uncertain.
The cave of Machpelah (Gen 23:9, 19); the Septuagint renders Machpelah as “the double cave.”

chapters.heading: The Testament of Reuben, on the Thoughts of the Mind

verses.text: A copy of the words of Simeon,{a} which he spoke to his sons before he died, in the hundred and twentieth year of his life, the year in which Joseph died.
His sons had come to visit him in his illness, and he gathered his strength and sat up, kissed them, and said to them,
“Listen, children, listen to Simeon your father, about everything I carry in my heart.
I was born to my father Jacob as his second son, and Leah{b} my mother called me Simeon, because the Lord heard her prayer.
I became very strong; I shrank from no task and was afraid of nothing.
My heart was hard, my liver unmoved, my insides without pity,
for courage, too, is given to people by the Most High, in soul and in body.
At that time I was jealous of Joseph, because our father loved him,
and I steeled my liver to kill him. The ruler of deceit sent the spirit of jealousy and blinded my mind, so that I did not look on him as a brother and did not spare Jacob my father.
But his God, the God of his fathers, sent His angel and rescued him from my hands.
For while I was away in Shechem{c} fetching ointment for the flocks, and Reuben was at Dothan,{d} where our supplies and all our stores were, our brother Judah sold him to the Ishmaelites.{e}
When Reuben came back he was grieved, for he had wanted to bring him safely to his father.
I was angry with Judah because he had let him go alive, and I stayed angry with him for five months.
Even so, God held me back and kept my hands from their work, for my right hand was half withered for seven days.
I knew, children, that this had come on me because of Joseph. I repented and wept, and I prayed to the Lord to restore my hand, so that I might keep away from all defilement, envy, and folly.
For I knew that I had planned an evil thing before the Lord and Jacob my father, through envying my brother Joseph.”
“Now, children, beware of the spirits of deceit and envy.
Envy rules the whole mind of a person and lets him neither eat nor drink nor do anything good.
It always urges him to destroy the one he envies; the envied person is always in bloom, while the envier withers.
For two years I afflicted my soul with fasting in the fear of the Lord, and I learned that the release from envy comes through the fear of God.
If someone runs to the Lord for refuge, the evil spirit runs away from him, and his mind becomes light.
From then on he feels with the one he envied, and does not condemn those who love him, and so his envy stops.”
“My father kept asking about me, because he saw me gloomy, and I said, ‘My liver aches.’
I mourned more than all the others, because I was to blame for the selling of Joseph.
When we went down to Egypt and he bound me as a spy, I knew I was suffering justly, and I did not grieve.
Joseph was a good man, with the spirit of God in him, tender-hearted and merciful. He held no grudge against me, but loved me as he loved the other brothers.

So beware, my children, of all jealousy and envy, and walk in simplicity of soul and in a good heart, keeping in mind your father’s brother, so that God may give you also grace, glory, and blessing on your heads, as you saw in him.
All his days he never reproached us about this matter, but loved us as his own soul, more than his own sons. He gave us glory, and granted us all riches, cattle, and crops.
You also, my dear children, should each love his brother with a good heart, and drive the spirit of envy out of you,

for it makes the soul savage and ruins the body. It brings anger and war to the mind, stirs it up to bloodshed, drives the mind out of its senses, and does not let people use their understanding. It even takes away sleep, and brings turmoil to the soul and trembling to the body.

Even in sleep, a jealous malice shows itself in dreams and eats the person up; with evil spirits it disturbs his soul, makes his body shake with fear, and wakes his mind in confusion. He looks to others like someone who has an evil, venomous spirit.”
“That is why Joseph was handsome in form and fair to look at: no evil lived in him. For the face shows what the spirit is stirred by.
Now, my children, make your hearts good before the Lord, and make your ways straight before people, and you will find favor with God and people.
Guard against sexual immorality, for it is the mother of all evils; it separates people from God and brings them near to Beliar.
I have seen in the writing of Enoch{f} that your sons, along with you, will be corrupted by sexual immorality, and will do wrong against Levi with the sword.
But they will not be able to stand against Levi, because he will fight the Lord’s war and will defeat all your camps.
You will be few in number, divided up among Levi and Judah, and no one of yours will hold rule, just as my father Jacob prophesied in his blessings.”
“See, I have told you everything beforehand, so that I am cleared of the sin of your souls.

If you remove envy and all stubbornness from you, my bones will blossom like a rose in Israel, and my flesh like a lily in Jacob. My fragrance will be like the fragrance of Lebanon, and holy cedars will multiply from me forever, and their branches will stretch far.
Then the seed of Canaan{g} will perish, and nothing will be left of Amalek;{h} all the Cappadocians will be destroyed, and all the Hittites will be wiped out.
Then the land of Ham{i} will fail and all its people will perish. Then the whole earth will rest from turmoil, and everything under heaven from war.
Then Shem{j} will be glorified, for the Lord God, the great one of Israel, will appear on the earth as a human being and save Adam{k} in him.
Then all the spirits of deceit will be handed over to be trampled, and people will rule over the evil spirits.
Then I will rise in joy and bless the Most High for His wonders, because God took a body, ate with humans, and saved them.”
“Now, my little children, obey Levi, and in Judah you will be set free. Do not exalt yourselves over these two tribes, for from them the salvation of God will rise for you.
The Lord will raise up from Levi a high priest, and from Judah a king, God and man. In this way He will save all the nations and the family of Israel.
For this reason I command you everything, so that you also may command your children, and they may keep these things through their generations.”
Simeon finished commanding his sons and fell asleep with his fathers, at the age of a hundred and twenty.
They laid him in a coffin of incorruptible wood, to carry his bones up to Hebron. They carried them up secretly during a war with the Egyptians.
For the Egyptians were guarding the bones of Joseph in the treasuries of the palace.

Their sorcerers had told them that when Joseph’s bones left, there would be darkness and gloom over all Egypt and a very great plague on the Egyptians, so that people would not recognize their own brothers even with a lamp.
Simeon’s sons mourned their father according to the custom of mourning, and they stayed in Egypt until the day they left Egypt, under Moses.{l}

notes.text: “Simeon” (Hebrew *Shimon*) is explained in Gen 29:33 by a wordplay on “heard,” as in “Yahweh has heard.” In the Greek the name is spelled Symeon.
“Leah” (Hebrew *Le’ah*) is of uncertain meaning; it may mean “wild cow” or “weary.”
“Shechem” (Hebrew *Shekhem*) means “shoulder” or “ridge.” The city stood in the hill country of Ephraim.
“Dothan” (Hebrew *Dothan*) is a town north of Shechem.
“Ishmaelites” are descendants of Ishmael, Abraham’s son, “God hears”; in Gen 37:25-28 they are the traders to whom Joseph is sold.
“Enoch” (Hebrew *Chanokh*) is explained as “dedicated” or “trained.” The writings ascribed to him are the books of 1 Enoch; the passage meant here is not found in the surviving texts.
“Canaan” (Hebrew *Kena’an*) is the land west of the Jordan and the name of its people; in Gen 9:25 Canaan is the son of Ham who is cursed.
“Amalek” (Hebrew *Amaleq*) is the desert people who attacked Israel at Rephidim (Exod 17:8-16) and were long treated as the model enemy.
“Ham” (Hebrew *Cham*) is one of Noah’s sons, whose line included Egypt and Canaan; the name may mean “hot” or “dark.”
“Shem” (Hebrew *Shem*) means “name.” He is the ancestor of the Semitic peoples, including Israel.
“Adam” (Hebrew *adam*) means “human being,” from the word for the ground, *adamah*. The line “save Adam in him” may be a Christian touch.
“Moses” (Hebrew *Mosheh*) is linked in Exod 2:10 with “drawing out.” He led Israel out of Egypt.

chapters.heading: The Testament of Simeon, on Envy

verses.text: A copy of the words of Levi,{a} everything he laid down for his sons, all that they should do and all that would happen to them until the day of judgment.
He was in good health when he called them to him, though it had been revealed to him that he was about to die. When they had gathered, he said to them,
“I, Levi, was conceived in Haran{b} and born there, and afterward I came with my father to Shechem.
I was quite young, about twenty years old, when, together with Simeon, I took vengeance on Hamor{c} for our sister Dinah.{d}

While we were shepherding in Abelmaul,{e} a spirit of the Lord’s understanding came on me, and I saw all people ruining their way, and I saw that injustice had built walls for itself, and lawlessness sat on towers.
I grieved over the human race and prayed to the Lord that I might be saved.
Then sleep fell on me, and I saw a high mountain. This is Mount Aspis in Abelmaul.
The heavens were opened, and an angel of God said to me, ‘Levi, come in.’
I went from the first heaven into the second, and there I saw water hanging between the one and the other.
I saw a third heaven, far brighter than the two, for it had a boundless height.
I said to the angel, ‘Why is this?’ and the angel said to me, ‘Do not be amazed at these things, for you will see four other heavens, brighter and beyond comparison, when you go up there.
You will stand near the Lord and be His servant, and you will announce His mysteries to people and proclaim the one who will redeem Israel.
Through you and Judah the Lord will be seen among people, saving in them every kind of human being.
Your life comes from the Lord’s portion, and He will be your field, vineyard, crops, gold, and silver.’”
“‘Listen, then, about the seven heavens. The lowest is gloomier than the rest because it is closest to all the injustice of people.
The second has fire, snow, and ice, ready for the day of the Lord’s command, in the righteous judgment of God. In it are all the spirits of the punishments, sent to take vengeance on the lawless.
In the third are the powers of the armies, appointed for the day of judgment, to take vengeance on the spirits of deceit and on Beliar. Those in the fourth, above these, are holy,
for in the highest of all the great Glory lives, in the Holy of Holies, above all holiness.
In the one below it are the angels of the Lord’s presence, who serve and make atonement before the Lord for all the sins of ignorance of the righteous.
They offer to the Lord a pleasing fragrance, a spiritual offering without blood.
In the one under that are the angels who carry the answers to the angels of the Lord’s presence.
In the one after that are thrones and powers, where hymns are always offered to God.
So when the Lord looks down on us, all of us are shaken. The heavens, the earth, and the depths shake before the face of His majesty,
but the sons of men, unaware of these things, sin and provoke the Most High.’”

“‘Know now that the Lord will bring judgment on the sons of men. When the rocks are split, the sun is put out, the waters dry up, the fire shrinks back, all creation is shaken, the unseen spirits melt, and Hades is plundered at the suffering of the Most High, people will not believe and will stay in their injustices; for this reason they will be judged with punishment.
The Most High has heard your prayer, that you be separated from injustice and become a son, servant, and minister of His presence.
You will shine the bright light of knowledge in Jacob, and you will be like the sun for all the seed of Israel.
Blessing will be given to you and to all your seed, until the Lord visits all the nations, in the compassion of His Son, forever. Yet your sons will lay hands on Him to hang Him on a pole.
For this reason counsel and understanding have been given to you, so that you may teach your sons about Him,
because whoever blesses Him will be blessed, and those who curse Him will perish.’”
“The angel opened the gates of heaven for me, and I saw the holy temple, and the Most High on a throne of glory.
He said to me, ‘Levi, I have given you the blessings of the priesthood, until I come and live among Israel.’
Then the angel brought me to the earth and gave me a shield and a sword and said, ‘Take vengeance at Shechem for Dinah, and I will be with you, for the Lord has sent me.’
At that time I finished off the sons of Hamor, as it is written on the tablets of heaven.
I said to him, ‘I beg you, Lord, tell me Your name, so that I may call on You in the day of trouble.’
He said, ‘I am the angel who pleads for the nation of Israel, so that they will not be struck down completely, because every evil spirit attacks them.’
After this I woke, as if I had been asleep, and blessed the Most High and the angel who pleads for the nation of Israel and for all the righteous.”
“As I was on my way to my father, I found a bronze shield; that is why the mountain’s name is Aspis, because it is near Gebal, to the right of Abila.
I kept these words in my heart.
I advised my father, and my brother Reuben, to tell the sons of Hamor that they must be circumcised, because I was zealous over the abomination they had done in Israel.
I killed Shechem first, and Simeon killed Hamor.
After that my brothers came and struck the city with the edge of the sword.
Our father heard of it and was angry and grieved, because they had accepted circumcision and afterward been killed, and in his blessings he spoke of us differently.
We had sinned, for we had done this against his judgment, and he became ill that day.
But I saw that God had pronounced evil against Shechem, because they wanted to do to Sarah what they had done to our sister Dinah, and the Lord stopped them.

In the same way they had persecuted Abraham our father when he was a foreigner, trampled his flocks when they swelled in number around him, and treated Jebla,{f} who was born in his household, savagely.
This is how they treated all foreigners, seizing their wives by force and driving the strangers out.
But the Lord’s wrath overtook them to the end.”
“I said to my father, ‘Do not be angry, sir, for through you the Lord will humble the Canaanites and give their land to you and your seed after you.
From today Shechem will be called a city of fools, for as one mocks a fool, so we have mocked them,
because they also did a foolish thing in Israel, defiling our sister.’
We took our sister from there, set out, and came to Bethel.{g}”
“There again I saw a vision like the earlier one, after we had spent seventy days.

I saw seven men in white clothing who said to me, ‘Get up, put on the robe of the priesthood, the crown of righteousness, the breastpiece of understanding, the long robe of truth, the plate of faith, the turban of the sign, and the ephod of prophecy.’
Each of them carried one of these things and put it on me, and they said, ‘From now on be a priest of the Lord, you and your seed, forever.’
The first anointed me with holy oil and gave me a staff of judgment.
The second washed me with pure water and fed me bread and wine, the holiest of holy things, and put a holy and glorious robe on me.
The third clothed me in fine linen, like an ephod.
The fourth put a belt on me like purple.
The fifth gave me a branch of rich olive.
The sixth put a wreath on my head.
The seventh put a priestly diadem on my head and filled my hands with incense, so that I could serve as priest to the Lord.
They said to me, ‘Levi, your seed will be divided into three offices, as a sign of the glory of the Lord who is to come.
The one who believes will be first, and no portion greater than his will be given.
The second will be in the priesthood.
The third will be given a new name, because a king will rise from Judah and set up a new priesthood, after the pattern of the nations, for all the nations.
His coming will be beyond words, as of a high prophet from the seed of Abraham our father.
Everything desirable in Israel will belong to you and to your seed. You will eat everything beautiful to see, and your seed will share out the Lord’s table.
From them will come high priests, judges, and scribes, for the holy place will be guarded by their word.’
I woke up and understood that this was like the earlier vision.
I hid this also in my heart and told it to no one on earth.”
“Two days later Judah and I went up to Isaac, following our father.
My father’s father blessed me according to all the words of the visions I had seen, but he did not want to go with us to Bethel.
When we came to Bethel, my father Jacob saw in a vision about me that I would be a priest to God for them.
He got up early in the morning and paid a tenth of everything to the Lord through me.
We came to Hebron to stay there.
Isaac called me constantly to remind me of the Lord’s law, as the angel of God had shown me.
He taught me the law of the priesthood, of sacrifices, whole burnt offerings, firstfruits, freewill offerings, and peace offerings.
Each day he instructed me and was busy with me before the Lord.
He said, ‘Child, beware of the spirit of sexual immorality. It will persist, and through your seed it is going to defile the holy things.
So take a wife for yourself while still young, one without blemish or defilement, who is not from the family of foreigners or nations.
Before you enter the holy things, bathe; while you sacrifice, wash; and when you finish the sacrifice, wash again.
Offer to the Lord from twelve trees that always have leaves, as Abraham also taught me.
From every clean animal and clean bird offer a sacrifice to the Lord.
From every firstfruit and from wine offer firstfruits, and salt every sacrifice.’”
“Now keep what I command you, children, because what I heard from my fathers I have told you.

I am innocent of all your ungodliness and transgression, which you will commit at the end of the ages against the Savior of the world, being ungodly, leading Israel astray, and stirring up great evils against it from the Lord.
You will act lawlessly along with Israel, so that Jerusalem will not be able to bear your wickedness, and the veil of the temple will be torn, so that it no longer covers your shame.
You will be scattered as captives among the nations and become a reproach and something to be trampled.
For the house the Lord chooses will be called Jerusalem, as the book of Enoch the righteous contains.”
“When I took a wife, I was twenty-eight years old. Her name was Milcah.{h}
She conceived and bore a son and called his name Gershom,{i} because we were sojourners in our land. For “Gershom” is written to mean “sojourning.”
I saw about him that he would not be in the first rank.
Kohath{j} was born in my thirty-fifth year, toward sunrise.
In a vision I saw him standing in the middle, on high, over the whole assembly.
For this reason I called his name Kohath, which means beginning of majesty and gathering.
She bore me Merari{k} in the fortieth year of my life. Because his mother had a hard labor, she called him Merari, which means “my bitterness,” because he too died.
Jochebed{l} was born in the sixty-fourth year, in Egypt, for I was honored then among my brothers.”
“Gershom took a wife and she bore him Libni and Shimei.
The sons of Kohath were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
The sons of Merari were Mahli and Mushi.
In my ninety-fourth year, Amram took my daughter Jochebed as his wife, for they were born on the same day, he and my daughter.
I was eight years old when I entered the land of Canaan, eighteen when I killed Shechem, nineteen when I became a priest, twenty-eight when I took a wife, and forty when I went into Egypt.
See, you are my children, my children, the third generation.
Joseph died in his hundred and eighteenth year.”
“Now, my children, I command you to fear our Lord with your whole heart and to walk in simplicity according to all His law.
Teach your children to read, too, so that they will have understanding all their lives, reading the law of God without ceasing.
For everyone who knows the law of God will be honored, and will not be a stranger wherever he goes.
He will gain many friends beyond his own parents, and many people will want to serve him and to hear the law from his mouth.
Do righteousness, my children, on the earth, so that you may find it in the heavens.
Sow good things in your souls, so that you find them in your lives. If you sow evil, you will reap every trouble and distress.

Gain wisdom in the fear of God, with diligence. For if there is captivity, and cities and lands are destroyed, and gold and silver and every possession are lost, no one can take away a wise person’s wisdom, except the blindness of ungodliness and the crippling of sin.
It will shine for him even among his enemies, in a foreign land he will find it a homeland, and in the midst of enemies he will be found a friend.
If he teaches these things and does them, he will sit on the throne with a king, as our brother Joseph did.”

“Now, children, I have learned from the writing of Enoch that at the end you will act ungodly against the Lord, laying hands on Him in every kind of wickedness, and your brothers will be ashamed because of you, and you will become a mockery to all the nations.
Our father Israel will be clean of the ungodliness of the high priests, who will lay their hands on the Savior of the world.
Heaven is purer than the earth, and you are the lights of heaven, like the sun and the moon.

What will all the nations do if you are darkened in ungodliness and bring a curse on our race, you through whom the light of the world was given among you to enlighten every person? You will want to destroy Him, teaching commands opposed to the decrees of God.
You will rob the Lord’s offerings, steal from His portions, and take the choice parts before sacrificing to the Lord, eating them with prostitutes in contempt.

In greed you will teach the Lord’s commands, defile married women, pollute the virgins of Jerusalem, and join with prostitutes and adulteresses. You will take the daughters of the nations as wives, purifying them with an unlawful purification, and your union will become Sodom and Gomorrah in ungodliness.
You will be puffed up over the priesthood, lifting yourselves above people; and not only that, but also puffed up against the commands of God,
you will mock the holy things and laugh at them in contempt.”
“For these reasons the temple the Lord chooses will be left empty in uncleanness, and you will be captives among all the nations,
and you will be an abomination among them, and receive reproach and everlasting shame from God’s righteous judgment.
All who see you will flee from you.
If it were not for Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob our fathers, not one of my seed would be left on the earth.”
“Now I have learned in the book of Enoch that for seventy weeks you will go astray, defile the priesthood, and pollute the sacrifices,
destroy the law and despise the words of the prophets. In perversity you will persecute righteous men, hate the godly, and loathe the words of the truthful.

You will call a man who renews the law in the power of the Most High a deceiver, and in the end, as you think, you will kill him, not knowing his rising, taking innocent blood on your heads in wickedness.
Because of him your holy places will be desolate, defiled down to the ground,
and you will have no clean place, but among the nations you will be a curse and a scattering, until He visits again and, having mercy, receives you in faith and water.”
“Since you have heard about the seventy weeks, now hear also about the priesthood.

In each jubilee there will be a priesthood. In the first jubilee the first one anointed to the priesthood will be great, and he will speak to God as to a father. His priesthood will be filled with the fear of the Lord, and in the day of his joy he will rise for the salvation of the world.
In the second jubilee the anointed one will be seized in sorrow over those he loves, and his priesthood will be honored and he will be glorified by all.
The third priest will be taken in grief.
The fourth will be in pain, because injustice will be piled on him in abundance, and all Israel will hate one another.
The fifth will be taken in darkness.
So also the sixth and the seventh.
In the seventh there will be such defilement as I cannot describe, before the Lord and people. Those who do these things will know it.
Because of this they will be in captivity and plunder, and their land and their possessions will be destroyed.
In the fifth week they will return to their desolate land and renew the house of the Lord.
In the seventh week the priests will come, idolaters, quarrelsome, lovers of money, proud, lawless, shameless, corrupters of boys and abusers of animals.”
“After the Lord’s punishment of them has come on the priesthood,
then the Lord will raise up a new priest, to whom all the words of the Lord will be revealed. He will carry out true judgment on the earth for many days.
His star will rise in heaven like a king’s, lighting the light of knowledge as the sun lights the day, and he will be magnified in the whole world until his taking up.
He will shine like the sun on the earth and remove all darkness from under heaven, and there will be peace in all the earth.

The heavens will rejoice in his days, the earth will be glad, the clouds will be joyful, and the knowledge of the Lord will be poured out on the earth like the water of the seas. The angels of the glory of the Lord’s presence will rejoice in him.
The heavens will be opened, and from the temple of glory sanctification will come on him with a fatherly voice, as from Abraham to Isaac.
The glory of the Most High will be spoken over him, and the spirit of understanding and sanctification will rest on him in the water.
He will give the majesty of the Lord to his sons in truth forever, and he will have no successor, from generation to generation, forever.
In his priesthood all sin will cease, the lawless will stop doing evil, and the righteous will find rest in him.
He will open the doors of Paradise and remove the threatening sword against Adam,
and give the holy ones to eat from the tree of life, and the spirit of holiness will be on them.
Beliar will be bound by him, and he will give his children authority to trample the evil spirits.
The Lord will rejoice over His children, and be pleased with His beloved ones forever.
Then Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob will be glad, and I will rejoice, and all the holy ones will put on gladness.”
“Now, my children, you have heard everything. Choose for yourselves either darkness or light, either the law of the Lord or the works of Beliar.”
We answered our father, “We will walk before the Lord, according to His law.”
Our father said, “The Lord is witness, His angels are witnesses, I am a witness, and you are witnesses to the word of your mouth.” And we said, “Witnesses.”
So Levi finished commanding his sons, stretched out his feet, and was gathered to his fathers, having lived a hundred and thirty-seven years.
They laid him in a coffin, and later they buried him in Hebron, beside Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

notes.text: “Levi” (Hebrew *Levi*) is explained in Gen 29:34 by a wordplay on “joined,” as the wife hopes her husband will be “joined” to her. The name is also the root of “Levite.”
“Haran” (Hebrew *Charan*) is the northern Mesopotamian city where Jacob lived with Laban; the name probably means “road” or “caravan stop.”
“Hamor” (Hebrew *Chamor*) means “donkey.” He was the ruler of Shechem in Gen 34.
“Dinah” (Hebrew *Dinah*) means “judgment” or “justice.” She is Jacob’s daughter by Leah.
“Abelmaul” is the Greek form of a place name; it is probably Abel-meholah or Abel-maim (“meadow of the waters”), in the north of the land.
“Jebla” is the form of the name in the Greek copies; the person is otherwise unknown. Some copies read differently.
“Bethel” (Hebrew *Beit-El*) means “house of God.” It lies in the hill country north of Jerusalem.
“Milcah” (Hebrew *Milkah*) means “queen.” The Greek here has a different form of the name.
“Gershom” (Hebrew *Gershom*) is explained in Exod 2:22 as “a sojourner there.”
“Kohath” (Hebrew *Qehat*) is of uncertain meaning; the text here explains it as “beginning of majesty and assembling.”
“Merari” (Hebrew *Merari*) is linked to the word for “bitter.”
“Jochebed” (Hebrew *Yokheved*) is probably “Yahweh is glory.” She is the mother of Moses in Exod 6:20.

chapters.heading: The Testament of Levi, on the Priesthood and Pride

verses.text: A copy of the words of Judah,{a} all that he said to his sons before he died.
They gathered and came to him, and he said to them,
“I was the fourth son born to my father, and my mother named me Judah, saying, ‘I give thanks to the Lord, who has given me a fourth son also.’
I was quick and eager in my youth, and obedient to my father in everything.
I blessed my mother and my mother’s sister.
When I grew to manhood, my father Jacob prayed over me, saying, ‘You will be king and will prosper in everything.’”
“The Lord gave me favor in all my work, in the field and at home.
When I saw that I had caught up with a deer, I seized it and made a meal for my father.
I caught gazelles by running, and overtook everything that lived in the plains. I overtook a wild mare and tamed it.
I killed a lion and took a young goat from its mouth. I took a bear by the foot and rolled it down a cliff, and any animal that turned on me I tore apart like a dog.
I ran down the wild boar, got ahead of it as I ran, and tore it to pieces.
A leopard in Hebron leaped on the dog; I seized it by the tail and flung it, and it burst apart in the territory of Gaza.
I grabbed a wild ox grazing in the country by its horns, spun it around until it was dizzy, threw it down, and killed it.”
“When the two kings of the Canaanites came in full armor against the flocks, with a large army, I ran out alone at King Shur,{b} gripped him, struck him on the shins, pulled him down, and killed him.
The other king, Taphue, was sitting on his horse; I killed him too, and so scattered the whole army.
King Achor, a man of giants, who shot arrows forward and backward from horseback, I lifted up; I hurled a sixty-pound stone{c} and struck his horse, and I killed him.
I fought Achor for two hours and killed him, and splitting his shield in two, I cut off his feet.
While I was stripping off his breastplate, eight of his companions began to attack me.
I wound my cloak around my hand, slung stones at them, and killed four of them; the rest fled.
Our father Jacob killed Beelesa, king of all the kings, a giant in strength, eighteen feet tall.{d}
Trembling fell on them, and they stopped fighting us.
That is why my father had no worry in the wars when I was with my brothers.
He had seen in a vision about me that an angel of power followed me in everything, so that I would not be defeated.”
“To the south we had a war greater than the one at Shechem. I drew up in battle line with my brothers and chased a thousand men, and killed two hundred of them and four kings.
I went up against them on the wall and killed two more kings.
In this way we freed Hebron and took all the plunder of the kings.”
“The next day we went to Areta, a strong city, walled and unapproachable, that threatened us with death.
Gad and I approached from the east side of the city; Reuben and Levi from the west and south.
The men on the wall, thinking we were alone, were drawn out against us.
So my brothers, secretly, from both sides, climbed the wall on pegs and entered the city while the people did not know.
We took it with the edge of the sword, and those who had fled to the tower we took by sawing the tower down with them in it.
As we were leaving, men from Taphu fell on our plunder, took it with our sons, and we engaged them as far as Taphu.
We killed them, burned the city, and plundered everything in it.”
“While I was at the waters of Chuzeba, the men from Jobel came against us for war.
We engaged them and killed them and their allies from Shelom, and we gave them no way through to reach us.
On the fifth day men from Machir attacked us to take the plunder. We met them in a hard fight and overcame them, though they were a strong crowd, and we killed them before they could climb the slope.
When we came to their city, their women rolled stones down on us from the top of the mountain where the city stood.
Simeon and I hid and came up behind them, took the high ground, and destroyed the whole city.”
“The next day we were told that the cities of the two kings were coming against us with a great crowd.
So Dan and I, pretending to be Amorites, came into their city as allies.
In the deep of night we opened the gates to our brothers when they came, and destroyed them all and everything they had; we plundered all their goods and tore down their three walls.
We came near to Thamna,{e} where all the hostile kings had taken refuge.
Then, insulted, I was furious and charged at them toward the summit, while they slung stones and shot arrows at me.
If my brother Dan had not fought beside me, they would have killed me.
We came on them in a rage and they all fled. They went another way and begged my father, and he made peace with them,
and we did them no harm, but made them subjects under treaty, and gave back all the plunder.
I built Thamna and my father built Rambael.
I was twenty years old when this war happened,
and the Canaanites were afraid of me and my brothers.”
“I also had many cattle, and had Hira the Adullamite{f} as my chief shepherd.
I went to him and saw Barsan, king of Adullam. He gave us a banquet, and in his friendliness he gave me his daughter Bathshua{g} as a wife.
She bore me Er, Onan, and Shelah.{h} The Lord killed the first two childless; Shelah lived, and you are his children.”
“For eighteen years we were at peace, our father and we, with his brother Esau,{i} and his sons with us, after we had come from Mesopotamia, from Laban.
When eighteen years were complete, in the fortieth year of my life, Esau, my father’s brother, came against us with a large and strong army.
Jacob’s bow struck him down, and he was carried dead to Mount Seir; and as he was being carried up to Iramna, he died.
We pursued the sons of Esau. They had a city with an iron wall and bronze gates, and we could not enter it, so we sat down around it and besieged them.

When they did not open after twenty days, I set up a ladder in their sight, with my shield over my head, and climbed up taking stones that weighed up to 225 pounds;{j} when I reached the top I killed four of their mighty men.
The next day Reuben and Gad went in and killed sixty others.
Then they asked us for terms of peace, and after consulting our father, we accepted them as tributaries.
They gave us 1,200 bushels{k} of wheat, 3,000 gallons{l} of oil, and 15,000 gallons{m} of wine, until we went down into Egypt.
“After this my son Er took Tamar,{n} the daughter of Aram, from Mesopotamia.
Er was wicked and was perplexed about Tamar, because she was not from the land of Canaan. An angel of the Lord killed him on the third night,
and he had not known her, through the scheming of his mother, for she did not want him to have children by her.
In the days of the wedding chamber I gave her to Onan as a husband; he too, in wickedness, did not know her, though he lived with her a year.
When I threatened him, he did go in to her, but he wasted the seed on the ground, following his mother’s order; and he also died in his wickedness.
I wanted to give Shelah to her too, but my wife Bathshua would not allow it. She acted wickedly toward Tamar, because Tamar was not one of the daughters of Canaan, as she herself was.”
“I knew that the race of Canaan was wicked, but the plans of youth blinded my heart.
When I saw her pouring wine, I was deceived by drunkenness and fell for her.
While I was away, she went and took a wife for Shelah from the land of Canaan.
When I learned what she had done, I cursed her in the anguish of my soul,
and she too died, through the wickedness of her sons.”
“After these things, when Tamar had been a widow for two years, she heard that I was going up to shear the sheep, and she dressed herself in bridal clothes and sat opposite the city by the gate.
It was the law of the Amorites that a woman about to marry should sit in prostitution seven days by the gate.
I was drunk at the waters of Chozeba, and because of the wine I did not recognize her. Her beauty deceived me, through the manner of her dress.
I turned aside to her and said, ‘Let me come in to you.’ She said, ‘What will you give me?’ I gave her my staff, my belt, and the diadem of my kingship, and when I went in to her she conceived.
Not knowing what she had done, I wanted to kill her; but she secretly sent the pledges, and she shamed me.
When I called her, I also heard the secret words I had spoken while sleeping with her in my drunkenness; and I could not kill her, because it was from the Lord.
I said, ‘Perhaps she did it deceitfully, having taken the pledge from someone else.’
But I never went near her again until my death, because I had done an abomination in all Israel.
People in the city even said there was no temple prostitute in the city, because she had come from another place and sat only a short while at the gate,
and she thought that no one knew I had gone in to her.
After this we went to Egypt, to Joseph, because of the famine.
I was forty-six years old and lived seventy-three years there.”
“Now listen, children, to your father about what I command you, and keep all my words, to do the decrees of the Lord and obey the command of the Lord God.
Do not follow your desires or the thoughts of your plans, in the pride of your heart, and do not boast in the deeds of your youthful strength, for this too is evil in the eyes of the Lord.

For I too boasted that in wars the face of a beautiful woman had never deceived me, and I used to reproach my brother Reuben about Bilhah, my father’s wife. Then the spirit of jealousy and sexual immorality fought against me, until I fell for Bathshua the Canaanite and for Tamar, who was promised to my sons.
I said to my father-in-law, ‘I will consult my father, and then I will take your daughter.’ He showed me, in the name of his daughter, an unlimited amount of gold, for he was a king.
He dressed her in gold and pearls and made her pour wine for us at the dinner, in the beauty of women.
The wine twisted my eyes, and pleasure darkened my heart.
I fell in love with her, gave in, and broke the Lord’s command and the command of my fathers, and I took her as my wife.
The Lord paid me back according to the plan of my heart, for I had no joy in her children.”
“Now, my children, do not get drunk on wine, for wine twists the mind away from the truth, throws in the anger of desire, and leads the eyes into error.
The spirit of sexual immorality has wine as its servant, to give pleasure to the mind; for these two together take away a person’s strength.

If someone drinks wine to drunkenness, he disturbs his mind with filthy thoughts toward sexual immorality and heats his body toward intercourse; and if the occasion of desire is present, he commits the sin and is not ashamed.
Such is wine, my children: the drunk respects no one.

See, it led me astray too, so that I was not ashamed before the crowd in the city, for in the sight of all I turned aside to Tamar, and I committed a great sin, and uncovered the cover of my sons’ shame.
After drinking wine I felt no shame before the command of God, and I took a Canaanite wife.
So a person who drinks wine needs understanding, my children, and this is the understanding about drinking: drink only as long as you keep your sense of shame.

If someone goes past this limit, wine invades the mind and produces the spirit of deceit. It makes the drunk speak shamefully and break the law without being ashamed, even boasting of his dishonor and thinking it good.”
“One who commits sexual immorality and is stripped of his kingship does not get out of it; he is enslaved to immorality, as I was stripped.
For I gave away my staff, that is, the support of my tribe; and my belt, that is, my strength; and the diadem, that is, the glory of my kingdom.
After repenting of these things, I took neither wine nor meat until old age, and I saw no happiness.
The angel of God showed me that women rule over both king and poor man forever,
and take from the king his glory, from the brave man his strength, and from the poor man the little support of his poverty.”
“So watch the limit with wine, my children. There are four evil spirits in it: of desire, of burning passion, of recklessness, of shameful gain.
If you drink wine in gladness, with respect and the fear of God, you will live. But if you drink without respect, and the fear of God is gone, then drunkenness follows and shamelessness creeps in.
If you do not drink at all, you will not sin in words of insult, quarreling, slander, and breaking the commands of God, and you will not perish before your time.

Wine even reveals the mysteries of God and people to outsiders, as I too revealed the commands of God and the mysteries of my father Jacob to the Canaanite Bathshua, things God had said not to reveal. Wine is also the cause of war and disorder.”
“I command you, my children, not to love money or look at the beauty of women, because it was for money and beauty that I was led astray to Bathshua the Canaanite.
I know that because of these two things, my descendants will be evil,
for they will change even the wise men among my sons and cause the kingdom of Judah to shrink, the kingdom the Lord gave me for obeying my father.
I never grieved the word of Jacob my father, for everything he said I did.
Abraham, my father’s father, blessed me to be king in Israel, and Isaac likewise blessed me in the same way.
I know that the kingdom will be established from me.”
“I have read in the books of Enoch the righteous what evils you will do in the last days.
So beware, my children, of sexual immorality and love of money; listen to Judah your father,
for these things pull people away from the law of God, blind the plans of the soul, teach pride, and do not let a person show mercy to his neighbor,
rob his soul of all goodness, hold him in toil and suffering, take his sleep away, and eat up his flesh,
hinder the sacrifices of God, forget blessings, do not listen to a prophet speaking, and are irritated by words of godliness.
For the person who serves two passions opposed to the commands of God cannot obey God, because they have blinded his soul, and he walks in the day as in the night.”
“My children, love of money leads to idols, for those led astray by money name as gods those who are not gods, and it makes whoever has it fall into madness.
Because of money I lost my children, and if it had not been for the repentance of my flesh, the humbling of my soul, and the prayers of my father Jacob, I would have died childless.
But the God of my fathers, the compassionate and merciful, forgave me because I acted in ignorance.
The ruler of deceit had blinded me, and I was ignorant, as a human being, as flesh corrupted by sins. I came to know my own weakness, though I had thought I was unbeatable.”
“Know, then, my children, that two spirits are at work in a person, the spirit of truth and the spirit of deceit.
In the middle is the understanding of the mind, which inclines whichever way it wishes.
The things of truth and the things of deceit are written on the human chest, and the Lord knows each one of them.
There is no time when a person’s deeds can escape notice, for they are written on the bones of his chest before the Lord.
The spirit of truth testifies to everything and accuses everyone, and the one who sinned is burned from within by his own heart, and cannot lift his face to the judge.”
“Now, children, love Levi so that you may last, and do not exalt yourselves over him, or you will be destroyed.
The Lord gave the kingship to me and the priesthood to him, and put the kingship under the priesthood.
He gave me the things of earth and gave him the things in heaven.
As heaven is above earth, so the priesthood of God is above the kingdom on earth.
For the Lord chose him over you to draw near to Him, to eat at His table, and to receive the firstfruits, the delicacies of the sons of Israel.

You will be to them like the sea. In the sea the just and the unjust are tossed by storms, some taken captive and some growing rich; so in you every kind of person: some endangered, taken captive, and others enriched by plunder.
Those who rule will be like sea monsters, swallowing people like fish. They will enslave free sons and daughters, and seize houses, fields, flocks, and goods;
they will feed the flesh of many, unjustly, to ravens and ibises, and they will advance in evil, lifting themselves up in greed.
There will be false prophets like storms, and they will persecute all the righteous.”
“The Lord will bring divisions against one another on them, and there will be constant wars in Israel,
and my kingdom will be brought to an end among foreigners, until the salvation of Israel comes, until the coming of the God of righteousness, so that Jacob and all the nations may rest in peace.
He will keep the strength of my kingdom forever. For the Lord swore to me with an oath that my kingdom and my seed’s would not fail all the days, forever.”
“I am very grieved, my children, over the shamelessness, sorcery, and idolatry you will commit against the kingdom, following mediums, omen-readers, and demons of deceit.
You will make your daughters musicians and public women, and you will mingle in the abominations of the nations.

For this the Lord will bring on you famine and plague, death and avenging sword, siege, dogs to tear your enemies apart, reproaches from friends, ruin and the rotting of eyes, the killing of children, the taking of wives, the plundering of possessions, the burning of the temple of God, the desolation of the land, and your own slavery among the nations.
They will castrate some of you to serve their wives as eunuchs.
When you return to the Lord with humble heart, repenting and walking in all the commands of God, the Lord will visit you in mercy and in love, bringing you out of the captivity of your enemies.”

“After this a star will rise for you from Jacob in peace, and a man will rise from my seed like the sun of righteousness, walking with the sons of men in gentleness and righteousness, and no sin will be found in him.
The heavens will be opened over him to pour out the blessing of the Holy Father’s spirit, and he will pour out the spirit of grace on you,
and you will be his sons in truth, and you will walk in his commandment, first and last.
This is the branch of God Most High, and this is the spring for the life of all flesh.
Then the scepter of my kingdom will shine, and a stem will grow from your root.
From it will rise a rod of righteousness for the nations, to judge and save all who call on the Lord.”

“After this Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob will rise to life, and I and my brothers will be chiefs, each with our scepter in Israel: Levi first, I second, Joseph third, Benjamin fourth, Simeon fifth, Issachar sixth, and so on in order, all of them.

The Lord blessed Levi; the angel of the presence, me; the powers of glory, Simeon; heaven, Reuben; the earth, Issachar; the sea, Zebulun; the mountains, Joseph; the tabernacle, Benjamin; the lights, Dan; delight, Naphtali; the sun, Gad; the olive tree, Asher.
There will be one people of the Lord and one language, and the spirit of deceit of Beliar will be no more, for he will be thrown into the fire forever.

Those who died in sorrow will rise in joy; those who were poor for the Lord’s sake will be made rich; those in need will be filled; those in weakness will be strong; and those who died for the Lord will be awakened to life.
The deer of Jacob will run in gladness, and the eagles of Israel will fly in joy. The ungodly will mourn, the sinners will weep, and all peoples will glorify the Lord forever.”
“So keep every law of the Lord, my children, for there is hope for all who make his way straight.”
He said to them, “I am a hundred and nineteen years old, and today I am dying before your eyes.
Let no one bury me in costly clothing or cut open my belly, because those who rule will do these things. And take me up to Hebron with you.”
After saying this Judah fell asleep, and his sons did everything he had commanded and buried him in Hebron with his fathers.

notes.text: “Judah” (Hebrew *Yehudah*) is explained in Gen 29:35 as “I will praise Yahweh.”
“Shur” and the other royal names in these chapters (Taphue, Achor, Beelesa) are unknown outside this book. The spellings follow the Greek.
The Greek says “sixty litrai,” a litra being the Roman pound of about 12 ounces (327 g), so about 43 pounds (19.6 kg).
The Greek says “twelve cubits”; at about 18 inches to the cubit this is about 18 feet (5.5 m).
“Thamna” is the Greek spelling of Timnah, the town in the hill country of Judah, which means “allotted portion.”
“Hira” (Hebrew *Chirah*) is the Adullamite friend of Judah in Gen 38:1. “Adullam” was a town in the lowland of Judah.
“Bathshua” (Hebrew *Bat-shua*) means “daughter of Shua” or “daughter of nobility.” In Gen 38:2 she is the Canaanite mother of Judah’s sons; the Greek spells the name “Bessous.”
“Er” (Hebrew *Er*) may mean “watchful”; “Onan” (Hebrew *Onan*) may mean “vigor”; “Shelah” (Hebrew *Shelah*) probably means “request” or “petition.” The Greek spells the last one “Shelom.”
“Esau” (Hebrew *Esav*) is Jacob’s twin brother, “hairy” or “made.”
The Greek says “up to three talents.” A talent was about 75 pounds (34 kg), so three talents is about 225 pounds (about 100 kg).
“Two hundred cors.” A cor was about 6 bushels (about 220 liters), so about 1,200 bushels (44,000 liters). The size of the cor varied.
“Five hundred baths.” A bath was about 6 gallons (about 22 liters), so about 3,000 gallons (11,000 liters).

“One thousand five hundred measures”; the Greek says only “measures” (*metra*), and the size is uncertain. If the measure was the metretes, about 10 gallons (39 liters), this would be about 15,000 gallons (59,000 liters).”
“Tamar” (Hebrew *Tamar*) means “date palm.”

chapters.heading: The Testament of Judah, on Courage, Greed, and Sexual Immorality

verses.text: A copy of the words of Issachar.{a} He called his sons and said to them, “Listen, children, to Issachar your father; give ear to the words of one beloved by the Lord.
I was born as the fifth son of Jacob, as the wages for mandrakes.
Jacob had brought mandrakes in from the field, and Rachel{b} met him and took them.
Reuben{c} was crying, and at the sound of him my mother Leah{d} came out.
These were sweet-smelling apples, which the land of Aram produced on high ground below a ravine of waters.
Rachel said, ‘I will not give them to you, for they will take the place of children for me.’
There were two apples. Leah said, ‘Let it be enough for you that you took the husband of my maidenhood. Will you take these too?’
Rachel said, ‘See, let Jacob be yours tonight in exchange for your son’s mandrakes.’
Leah said to her, ‘Do not boast or glorify yourself. Jacob is mine, and I am the wife of his youth.’
Rachel said, ‘What of it? He was betrothed to me first, and for my sake he served our father fourteen years.
What am I to do to you, since deceit and cunning have multiplied among people, and deceit advances on the earth? Otherwise you would not be looking on Jacob’s face;
for you are not his wife, but were brought in by trickery in my place.
My father deceived me, and moved me aside that night and did not let me see; for if I had been there, this would not have happened.’
Then Rachel said, ‘Take one mandrake, and in exchange for the one I will hire him out to you for one night.’
So Jacob knew Leah, and she conceived and bore me; and because of the wages I was called Issachar.”
“Then an angel of the Lord appeared to Jacob and said that Rachel would bear two children, because she had spat on a husband’s company and had chosen self-control.

If my mother Leah had not given up the two apples in exchange for company, she would have borne eight sons. That is why she bore six, and Rachel the two, because the Lord visited her over the mandrakes.
He saw that she wanted to be with Jacob for the sake of children and not for love of pleasure.
For the next day she gave Jacob up again, in order to get the other mandrake as well. That is why the Lord listened to Rachel over the mandrakes;
for although she longed for them, she did not eat them, but dedicated them in the house of the Lord, bringing them to the priest of the Most High who was there at that time.”
“When I grew to manhood, my children, I walked in uprightness of heart, and became a farmer for my fathers and my brothers, and brought in produce from the fields in its season.
My father blessed me, seeing that I walked in simplicity.
I was not meddlesome in my actions, nor was I wicked or envious toward my neighbor.
I never spoke against anyone, nor criticized any person’s way of life, but walked with simple eyes.
For this reason I took a wife only at thirty, because toil consumed my strength; I did not think about a woman’s pleasure, but from the labor sleep overcame me,

and my father was always glad over my simplicity. Whenever I worked hard, I first brought every fruit and every first produce to the Lord through the priest, then to my father, and only then took some myself.
The Lord doubled the good things in my hands. Jacob also knew that God worked together with my simplicity,
for to every poor person and every afflicted person I gave of the good things of the land, in simplicity of heart.”
“Now listen to me, children, and walk in simplicity of heart, for I have seen in it everything that pleases the Lord.
The simple person does not desire gold; he does not take advantage of his neighbor; he does not crave a variety of foods; he does not want expensive clothing;
he does not plan to live a long time, but only waits for the will of God.
The spirits of error have no power against him. He does not even look at a woman’s beauty, so that he will not pollute his mind with perversion.
Envy does not enter his thoughts; jealousy does not waste away his soul; and he does not scheme for gain out of insatiable greed.

He walks in uprightness of life and sees everything in simplicity, not letting his eyes take in wickedness from the world’s error, so that he will not see any of the Lord’s commands in a twisted way.”
“So keep the law of God, my children, and acquire simplicity, and walk in innocence, not prying into the Lord’s commands or into the neighbor’s affairs,
but love the Lord and your neighbor, and show mercy to the poor and the sick.
Bend your backs to farming, and work at the tasks of the land in every kind of cultivation, bringing gifts to the Lord with thanksgiving;
for the Lord has blessed you with the first fruits of the earth, as he blessed all the holy ones from Abel until now.
No other portion has been given to you than that of the richness of the earth, whose fruits come with labor.
For our father Jacob blessed me with the blessings of the earth and of the first fruits.
Levi and Judah were glorified by the Lord among the sons of Jacob. For the Lord assigned them their lots, giving the priesthood to the one and the kingship to the other.
So obey them, and walk in the simplicity of your father; for to Gad it was given to destroy the raiding bands that attack Israel.”

“I know, my children, that in the last times your sons will abandon simplicity and cling to greed; leaving innocence, they will approach wickedness; abandoning the commands of the Lord, they will cling to Beliar;{e}
leaving farming, they will follow their own wicked plans. They will be scattered among the nations and will serve their enemies.
So tell these things to your children, so that if they sin, they will turn back to the Lord the sooner;
for he is merciful and will rescue them, to bring them back to their land.”
“I am a hundred and twenty-two years old, and I have not known any sin that deserves death.
Apart from my wife, I have known no other woman. I never committed sexual immorality by lifting my eyes.
I never drank wine to be led astray. I never longed for anything my neighbor desired.
There was no deceit in my heart. No lie went up through my lips.
I groaned with every person in pain, and shared my bread with the poor. I never ate alone. I never moved a boundary. I practiced godliness and truth all my days.
I loved the Lord with all my strength; and I loved every person as I did my own children.

Do these things too, my children, and every spirit of Beliar will flee from you, and no action of wicked people will rule over you. You will bring every wild beast under your power, having with you the God of heaven, who walks with people in simplicity of heart.”
He commanded them to carry him up to Hebron and bury him there in the cave with his fathers.
Then he stretched out his feet and died, the fifth son, in a good old age, with every limb sound and strength intact, and he slept the sleep of eternity.

notes.text: “Issachar” (Hebrew *Yissakhar*) is explained in Gen 30:18 as “hire” or “reward,” from the bargain over the mandrakes told in the next verses.
“Rachel” (Hebrew *Rakhel*) means “ewe.”
“Reuben” (Hebrew *Re’uven*) is explained in Gen 29:32 as “See, a son!”
“Leah” (Hebrew *Le’ah*) may mean “wild cow” or “weary.”
“Beliar” is a name for the chief evil spirit, from Hebrew *Beliyya’al*, “worthlessness.”

chapters.heading: The Testament of Issachar, on Simplicity

verses.text: A copy of the words of Zebulun,{a} which he laid down for his children in the hundred and fourteenth year of his life, thirty-two years after the death of Joseph.
He said to them, “Listen to me, sons of Zebulun; pay attention to the words of your father.
I am Zebulun, a good gift to my parents. When I was born our father grew very rich, in flocks and herds, when he took his share by means of the striped rods.
I do not know, my children, that I have sinned in my days, except in thought.
Nor do I remember doing any lawless act, except the ignorance I showed over Joseph, for I covered up for my brothers and did not tell my father what had happened.
I wept a great deal in secret, for I was afraid of my brothers, because they had all agreed together that if anyone revealed the secret, he would be killed with the sword.
When they wanted to kill Joseph, I pleaded with them at length, in tears, not to commit this lawless act.”
“Simeon and Gad came at Joseph to kill him. Falling on his face, Joseph said to them,
‘Have pity on me, my brothers; have mercy on the heart of Jacob our father. Do not lay your hands on me to shed innocent blood, for I have not sinned against you.
And if I have sinned, punish me with discipline, but do not lay your hand on me, for the sake of Jacob our father.’
As he spoke these words, I was moved to pity and began to weep; my liver dissolved within me, and the whole substance of my insides melted into my soul.
Joseph wept, and I with him; my heart pounded, and the joints of my body gave way, so that I could not stand.
When he saw me weeping with him, and the others coming to kill him, he took refuge behind me, begging them.
Reuben stood up and said, ‘Brothers, let us not kill him, but throw him into one of these dry pits, which our fathers dug and found no water.’
For this reason the Lord had kept water from rising in them, so that Joseph would be preserved.
The Lord did this until they sold him to the Ishmaelites.”
“I had no share in the price of Joseph, children,
but Simeon and Gad and our other six brothers took the price of Joseph and bought sandals for themselves, their wives, and their children, saying,
‘We will not eat it, since it is the price of our brother’s blood, but we will trample it, because he said he would be king over us. Let us see what becomes of his dreams.’
For this reason it is written in the writing of the law of Enoch{b} that whoever does not want to raise up seed for his brother is to have his sandal taken off and be spat on in the face.
Joseph’s brothers did not want their brother to live, and the Lord took the sandal off them in Joseph’s case.
For when they came to Egypt, Joseph’s servants took their sandals off in front of the gate, and so they bowed down to Joseph in the manner of Pharaoh’s court.
They not only bowed to him but were spat on, falling down right away in front of him, and so they were shamed in front of the Egyptians.
After this the Egyptians heard about all the evil we had done to Joseph.”
“After this, they sat down to eat.
I tasted nothing for two days and two nights, in pity for Joseph. Judah did not eat with them but kept watch at the pit, for he was afraid Simeon and Gad would jump up and kill him.
When they saw me too not eating, they appointed me to guard him until he was sold.
He spent three days and three nights in the pit, and so he was sold without having eaten.
When Reuben heard that Joseph had been sold in his absence, he tore his clothes and mourned, saying, ‘How can I look on the face of Jacob my father?’
He took the money and ran after the merchants, but found no one; they had left the main road and gone by a shortcut through cave-ridden country.
Reuben ate no bread that day. Dan came to him and said,
‘Do not cry and do not mourn, for I have found what we can tell our father Jacob.
Let us slaughter a kid of the goats and dip Joseph’s tunic in its blood, and say, “See whether this is your son’s tunic.”’
They had stripped off the tunic of our father that Joseph was wearing when he was about to be sold, and dressed him in a slave’s old cloak.
Simeon had the tunic and did not want to give it up, wishing to hack it with his sword, angry that Joseph lived and he had not killed him.
All of us together stood up against him and said that if he did not hand it over, we would say that he alone had done this evil in Israel.
So he gave it over, and they did as Dan had said.”
“Now, my children, I will tell you to keep the commands of the Lord, to show mercy toward your neighbor, and to have compassion toward everyone, not only toward people, but also toward animals.
For because of these things the Lord blessed me, and when all my brothers were sick, I passed through without illness; for the Lord knows each one’s purpose.
So have mercy in your hearts, my children, because as someone treats his neighbor, so the Lord will treat him.
The sons of my brothers were sick and were dying because of Joseph, since they showed no mercy in their hearts; but my sons were kept healthy, as you know.
When I was in Canaan, at the seacoast, I used to catch fish for Jacob my father; and while many were drowning in the sea, I remained unharmed.”
“I was the first to make a boat to sail on the sea, because the Lord gave me understanding and wisdom for it.
I set a rudder at the back, and spread a sail on an upright pole in the middle.
Sailing in it along the shores, I fished for the house of my father until we came to Egypt.
From my catch I gave to every stranger out of compassion.
If someone was a stranger, or sick, or old, I would boil the fish, prepare them well, and offer them to all according to each one’s need, sharing their pain along with them.
For this reason the Lord also gave me plenty of fish to catch; whoever gives to his neighbor receives many times more from the Lord.
I fished for five years, giving to everyone I saw and providing enough for the whole house of my father.
In summer I fished; in winter I shepherded with my brothers.”
“Now I will tell you what I did. I saw a man in distress, naked in the winter cold. In pity for him, I secretly took a cloak from my own house and gave it to the man in distress.
You too, my children, from what God provides you, show mercy to all without distinction, and give to everyone with a good heart.
If you do not have anything to give to the needy at that time, share their pain with a heart of mercy.
I know that my hand did not find anything to give to someone in need at the moment, and still I walked with him nearly a mile{c} and wept; my heart turned inside me in sympathy for him.”
“So you too, my children, have compassion in mercy for every person, so that the Lord will also have compassion and mercy on you;
for in the last days God will send his compassion on the earth, and wherever he finds hearts of mercy, he will live in them.
To the degree that a person has compassion on his neighbor, the Lord will have that much on him.
When we went down to Egypt, Joseph did not hold a grudge against us; and when he saw me, he was moved with compassion.
Looking to him, you too, my children, be free of grudges, and love one another, and do not keep count of each other’s wrongs;
