for this breaks up unity, scatters every family, and troubles the soul. A person who holds a grudge has no heart of mercy.”
“Look at the water: it goes in one direction, sweeping along stones, sticks, and sand.
If it is divided into many streams, the earth swallows them up, and they become worth nothing.
You too will be like this if you are divided.
Do not be split into two heads, for everything the Lord made has one head. He gave two shoulders, hands, and feet, but all the limbs obey the one head.
I learned in the writing of my fathers that in the last days you will fall away from the Lord and be divided in Israel; you will follow two kings, commit every abomination, and worship every idol;
your enemies will take you captive, and you will live among the nations in all kinds of weakness, affliction, and pain of soul.

After that you will remember the Lord and repent, and he will bring you back, because he is merciful and compassionate and does not hold evil against human beings, since they are flesh and the spirits of error deceive them in everything they do.

After that the Lord himself will rise on you, the light of righteousness, with healing and compassion in his wings. He will redeem every captive of the sons of men from Beliar, and every spirit of error will be trampled. He will turn all the nations to jealousy for him, and you will see God in the form of a man, whom the Lord will choose, whose name is Jerusalem.
And again, by the wickedness of your words, you will provoke him to anger, and you will be rejected until the time of the end.”
“Now, my children, do not grieve that I am dying, or be cast down because I am leaving you.
I will rise again among you as a leader among his sons, and I will rejoice among my tribe, with all who kept the law of the Lord and the commands of Zebulun their father.
But on the ungodly the Lord will bring eternal fire, and he will destroy them through the generations.
I am running to my rest, as my fathers did.
You, fear the Lord your God with all your strength all the days of your life.”
After he said this, he fell asleep in a good sleep, and his sons laid him in a coffin.
Later they carried him up to Hebron and buried him with his fathers.

notes.text: “Zebulun” (Hebrew *Zevulun*) is explained in Gen 30:20 as “honor” or “dwelling.”
“Enoch” (Hebrew *Chanokh*) means “dedicated” or “initiated.” The “law of Enoch” is not found in the Hebrew Bible; the rule resembles Deut 25:5–10, and the reference may be to the books of Enoch.
“Seven stadia.” A stadion was about 607 feet (185 m), so seven stadia is about 0.8 mile (1.3 km).

chapters.heading: The Testament of Zebulun, on Compassion and Mercy

verses.text: A copy of the words of Dan,{a} which he spoke to his sons in the last days of his life, in the hundred and twenty-fifth year of his life.
He called his clan together and said, “Listen, sons of Dan, to my words; pay attention to the speech of your father’s mouth.
I have tested in my heart and through my whole life that truth with right dealing is good and pleasing to God, and that lying and anger are evil, because they teach a person every wickedness.
I confess to you today, my children, that in my heart I was pleased about the death of Joseph, a true and good man,
and I rejoiced at the sale of Joseph, because his father loved him more than us.
For the spirit of jealousy and arrogance said to me, ‘You too are his son.’
One of the spirits of Beliar worked with me, saying, ‘Take this sword, and with it kill Joseph; when he is dead, your father will love you.’
This was the spirit of anger that persuaded me to suck Joseph dry, as a leopard sucks dry a kid.
But the God of Jacob our father did not hand him over into my hands so that I could find him alone, nor did he let me carry out this lawless deed, which would have broken the two scepters in Israel.”
“Now, my children, I am dying, and I tell you in truth that unless you guard yourselves against the spirit of lying and of anger, and love truth and patience, you will perish.
There is blindness in anger, my children, and no angry person sees a face truly.

Whether it is a father or a mother, he treats them as enemies; if a brother, he does not know him; if a prophet of the Lord, he disobeys; if a righteous man, he does not see him; a friend he does not recognize.
For the spirit of anger wraps him in the nets of error, blinds his natural eyes, darkens his mind with lying, and gives him a vision of his own.
How does it wrap his eyes? With hatred in the heart, and it gives him a heart of his own against his brother, out of envy.”
“Anger is evil, my children, for it becomes a soul to the soul itself.
It takes the angry person’s body as its own and rules his soul, giving his body power of its own to do every lawless act;
and when the soul does it, anger justifies what was done, because he does not see.

So the person who is angry, if he is powerful, has a threefold strength in his anger: one through his power and the help of those who serve him; the second through wealth, persuading and winning by injustice; the third the natural strength of his body, doing the evil himself.
If the angry person is weak, he has double the strength his nature gives, for anger always helps such people in lawless acts.
This spirit always walks with lying at the right hand of Satan, so that his deeds are done in cruelty and falsehood.”
“So understand the power of anger, that it is empty.
First it provokes with a word; then through deeds it gives strength to the one who is stirred up, and with bitter losses it disturbs his judgment; and so it rouses his soul in great anger.
So when someone speaks against you, do not be moved to anger; and if anyone praises you as good, do not be puffed up or changed, either toward pleasure or toward appearance.
For first it delights the ear, and so it sharpens the mind to grasp what has been stirred up; and then, angry, one thinks he is rightly furious.
If you fall into a loss or the destruction of something, my children, do not be troubled; for this same spirit makes you long for what was lost, so that you become angry through the longing.
If you suffer loss willingly, do not be sad, for out of sadness it raises anger together with lying.
Anger and lying are a two-faced evil, and they join together to throw the mind into confusion. When the soul is continually troubled, the Lord withdraws from it, and Beliar rules it.”
“So keep the Lord’s commands, my children, and guard his law; keep away from anger and hate lying, so that the Lord may live in you and Beliar may flee from you.
Speak truth, each one to his neighbor, and you will not fall into pleasure and disorder, but will be in peace, having the God of peace, and war will not overpower you.
Love the Lord all your life, and one another with a true heart.

For I know that in the last days you will depart from the Lord and become offended at Levi and set yourselves against Judah; but you will not be able to prevail against them. An angel of the Lord leads each, because Israel will stand through them.

When you depart from the Lord, you will walk in every evil, committing the abominations of the nations, going off with the wives of lawless people, while the spirits of error work in you in every wickedness.

I read in the book of Enoch the righteous that your ruler is Satan, and that all the spirits of sexual immorality and pride will obey Levi, in order to sit constantly beside the sons of Levi and make them sin before the Lord.
My sons will come near to Levi and sin together with them in everything; and the sons of Judah will be greedy, seizing what belongs to others like lions.
For this reason you will be led away with them into captivity, and there you will receive all the plagues of Egypt and all the evils of the nations;
and so when you return to the Lord you will receive mercy, and he will bring you into his sanctuary, calling out peace to you.
Out of the tribe of Judah and Levi the salvation of the Lord will rise for you; he himself will make war on Beliar, and will give the vengeance of victory to those at our borders.
He will take the captives from Beliar, the souls of the holy ones, and will turn disobedient hearts to the Lord, and will give everlasting peace to those who call on him,
and the holy ones will rest in Eden, and the righteous will rejoice in the new Jerusalem, which will be to the glory of God forever.

Jerusalem will no longer endure desolation, nor will Israel be taken captive, because the Lord will be in the middle of it, living with people, and the Holy One of Israel will reign over them in humility and poverty; and whoever believes in him will reign in truth in the heavens.”
“Now fear the Lord, my children, and watch yourselves against Satan and his spirits.
Draw near to God and to the angel who intercedes for you, for he is a mediator between God and humanity for the peace of Israel. He will stand against the kingdom of the enemy.
For this reason the enemy is eager to trip up all who call on the Lord.
He knows that on the day Israel believes, the kingdom of the enemy will be brought to an end.
The angel of peace himself will strengthen Israel, so that it does not fall into the final evil.
In the time of Israel’s lawlessness the Lord will withdraw from them, and will go after those who do his will, because among the angels there will be none like him.
His name will be Savior in every place in Israel and among the nations.
So keep yourselves, my children, from every evil deed; throw away anger and all lying, and love truth and patience,

and pass on to your children what you heard from your father, so that the Father of the nations may receive you; for he is true and patient, gentle and humble, and teaches the law of God by his works.
So keep away from all injustice and cling to the righteousness of the law of the Lord.
And bury me near my fathers.”
After saying this, he kissed them and fell asleep with the sleep of eternity.
His sons buried him, and afterward carried his bones up near Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
But as Dan prophesied to them, that they would forget the law of their God and be alienated from the land of their inheritance and from the race of Israel and their family, so it happened.

notes.text: “Dan” (Hebrew *Dan*) means “he judged,” as in Gen 30:6, “God has judged me.”

chapters.heading: The Testament of Dan, on Anger and Lying

verses.text: A copy of the testament of Naphtali,{a} which he laid down at the time of his end, in the hundred and thirty-second year of his life.
When his sons had gathered in the seventh month (September–October){b} on the fourth day of the month, while he was in good health, he gave a dinner and a drinking party.
After he woke up the next morning, he told them he was dying; but they did not believe him.
Blessing the Lord, he insisted that he would die after the dinner of the day before.
Then he began to say to his sons, “Listen, my children, sons of Naphtali; listen to the words of your father.
I was born of Bilhah.{c} Because Rachel acted shrewdly and gave Bilhah to Jacob in her place, and Bilhah bore me on Rachel’s thighs, I was called Naphtali.
Rachel loved me because I was born on her thighs; and when I was a tender little thing she would kiss me, saying, ‘May I see a brother of yours from my own womb, like you.’
So Joseph was like me in everything, following Rachel’s prayers.
My mother Bilhah was the daughter of Rotheus, brother of Deborah, Rebekah’s nurse, who was born on the same day as Rachel.
Rotheus was of the family of Abraham, a Chaldean, God-fearing, free and noble.
He was taken captive and bought by Laban, who gave him his slave woman Aina as a wife; she bore a daughter, and he called her Zilpah, after the name of the village where he had been taken captive.
After that she bore Bilhah, and he said, ‘My daughter is eager for something new, for as soon as she was born she was in a hurry to nurse.’”
“Because I was light on my feet like a deer, my father Jacob assigned me to every errand and message; and he even blessed me as a deer.
As the potter knows a vessel, how much it holds, and brings clay accordingly, so the Lord makes the body to match the spirit, and fits the spirit to the power of the body.
Nothing is left over, not a third of a hair’s breadth from one to another; for all creation of the Most High is by weight, measure, and rule.
As the potter knows the use of each vessel and what it suits, so the Lord knows the body: how far it will last in good, and when it begins in evil.
There is no creature and no thought that the Lord does not know, for he made every person in his own image.

As his strength is, so is his work; as his mind, so his work; as his choice, so his action; as his heart, so his mouth; as his eye, so his sleep; as his soul, so his word, either in the law of the Lord or in the law of Beliar.

Just as there is a separation between light and darkness, sight and hearing, so there is a separation between man and man, and between woman and woman; and one cannot say that one is the same as another in face or likeness.

God made everything good in order: he put the five senses in the head, joined the neck to the head, and hair for glory; then the heart for understanding, the belly for sorting what the stomach takes in, the windpipe for health, the liver for anger, the gall for bitterness, the spleen for laughter, the kidneys for cunning, the loin muscles for power, the ribs as a case, the hip for strength, and so on.
So, my children, be in order for good things in the fear of God, and do nothing disorderly in contempt, or out of its proper time.
If you tell the eye to hear, it cannot; so you will not be able to do the works of light while in darkness.”

“So do not hurry, in greed, to corrupt your actions, or to deceive your souls with empty words; for if you are silent with a pure heart, you will be able to hold to the will of God and throw off the will of the devil.
The sun, the moon, and the stars do not change their order; so you, do not change the law of God by disorder in your actions.
The nations went astray and left the Lord; they changed their order and followed stones and sticks, following spirits of error.

You must not be like that, my children, you who know in the sky, on earth, and in the sea, and in all that is made, the Lord who made all of it, so that you do not become like Sodom, which changed the order of its nature.
In the same way the Watchers changed the order of their nature, whom the Lord also cursed at the flood, and because of them he made the earth uninhabited and fruitless.”
“I say this, my children, because I read in the holy writing of Enoch{d} that you too will depart from the Lord, going after every evil of the nations, and will commit every lawless act of Sodom.
The Lord will bring captivity on you, and there you will serve your enemies, and be covered with every ill-treatment and affliction, until the Lord has used up all of you.
After you have become few and small, you will return and know the Lord your God; and he will bring you back into your land, in his great mercy.
It will happen that when they arrive in the land of their fathers, they will again forget the Lord and become ungodly,
and the Lord will scatter them over the face of all the earth, until the compassion of the Lord comes, a man doing righteousness and showing mercy to all, far and near.”
“In the fortieth year of my life, I saw on the Mount of Olives, east of Jerusalem, that the sun and the moon stood still.
There was Isaac, my father’s father, saying to us, ‘Run and grab hold, each as you are able; whoever catches them will have the sun and the moon.’
We all ran together; Levi seized the sun, and Judah got there first and caught the moon, and both of them were lifted up with them.
When Levi was like the sun, a young man gave him twelve palm branches; and Judah was bright like the moon, and under his feet were twelve rays.
Levi and Judah ran to each other and held each other.
Then there was a bull on the earth, with two great horns and an eagle’s wings on its back; we wanted to catch it, but could not.
Joseph got there first, caught it, and went up with it on high.

I saw that I was there somewhere, and a holy writing appeared to us, saying: ‘Assyrians, Medes, Persians, Elymeans, Gelachaeans, Chaldeans, and Syrians will inherit, in captivity, the twelve tribes of Israel.’”
“Seven months later I saw our father Jacob standing by the sea of Jamnia, and we his sons were with him.
A ship came sailing, full of dried fish, without sailors or pilot; and on the ship was written ‘Jacob.’
Our father said to us, ‘Let us get on our ship.’
When we went in, a violent storm came, a whirlwind of great wind, and our father, who had been holding our necks, was torn away from us.
We were tossed in the storm and carried out to sea; the ship filled with water, battered by huge waves, until it began to break up.
Joseph fled on a small boat; we were separated too, onto ten planks; Levi and Judah were on the same one.
So we were all scattered, to the ends of the earth.
Levi, wrapped in sackcloth, prayed to the Lord for all of us.
When the storm stopped, the vessel reached land, as if in peace.
Then our father Jacob came, and we rejoiced together.”
“I told these two dreams to my father, and he said to me, ‘These must be fulfilled in their time, after Israel endures many things.’
Then my father said to me, ‘I believe that Joseph is alive; for I always see that the Lord is counting him with you.’
Weeping, he said, ‘You are alive, Joseph my child, and I do not see you, and you do not see Jacob who fathered you.’
He made us weep, too, with these words. I burned inside to tell him that Joseph had been sold, but I was afraid of my brothers.”
“Now, my children, I have shown you the last times, how all will happen in Israel.
So command your children to unite themselves to Levi and Judah. For through Judah salvation will rise for Israel, and in him Jacob will be blessed.
Through his scepter God will appear, living among people on the earth, to save the race of Israel; and he will gather the righteous from the nations.

If you do what is good, my children, people and angels will bless you; God will be glorified through you among the nations, the devil will flee from you, wild animals will fear you, and angels will hold on to you.
Just as someone who raises a child well has a good memory of it, so for a good deed there is a good memory with God.

But anyone who does not do good, people and angels will curse; God will be dishonored through him among the nations; the devil will claim him as his own tool; every wild animal will master him; and the Lord will hate him.
The commands of the law are twofold, and they are fulfilled with skill.
There is a time for a man’s intercourse with his wife, and a time of self-control for his prayer.
These are two commands, and if they do not happen in their proper order, they bring sin. It is the same with the other commands.
So be wise in God and prudent, knowing the order of his commands and the rules for every matter, so that the Lord will love you.”
After giving them many such commands, he asked them to carry his bones to Hebron and bury him with his fathers.
Then, after eating and drinking with a cheerful heart, he covered his face and died.
His sons did everything that their father Naphtali had commanded them.

notes.text: “Naphtali” (Hebrew *Naftali*) is explained in Gen 30:8 as “my wrestling,” from Rachel’s saying “I have wrestled with my sister.”

The Greek says “the seventh month, the fourth day of the month.” Counted from spring, the seventh month of the Hebrew calendar (Tishri) falls in September–October, so the fourth day is early in that span.
“Bilhah” (Hebrew *Bilhah*) is the maid of Rachel; the meaning of the name is uncertain.
“Enoch” is the patriarch whose books (the Books of Enoch) circulated in this period. The “holy writing of Enoch” is probably 1 Enoch, though the exact passage is not found there.

chapters.heading: The Testament of Naphtali, on Natural Order

verses.text: A copy of the testament of Gad,{a} which he spoke to his sons in the hundred and twenty-seventh year of his life, saying,
“I was the seventh son born to Jacob, and I was brave with the flocks.

I kept watch over the flock at night, and when a lion, a wolf, a leopard, a bear, or any wild animal came against the flock, I chased it down, caught its foot in my hand, spun it around until it was dizzy, and hurled it about a quarter of a mile,{b} and so killed it.
Joseph was shepherding with us for about thirty days, and, being delicate, he fell ill from the heat,
and went back to Hebron to his father, who made him lie down near him, because he loved him.
Joseph told our father that the sons of Zilpah and Bilhah were slaughtering the best animals and eating them, against the judgment of Judah and Reuben.

For he had seen that I snatched a lamb out of the bear’s mouth, and killed the bear, and slaughtered the lamb, which I felt sorry about because it could not live, and we ate it; and he told our father.
I held a grudge against Joseph over this matter until the day he was sold into Egypt.

The spirit of hatred was in me, and I did not want to see Joseph with my eyes or hear him with my ears. He had reproved us to our faces because we were eating the animals without Judah; and everything he said to his father, his father believed.”
“I confess my sin now, children: many times I wanted to kill him, because I hated him to the depth of my soul, and I had no mercy in my insides for him at all.
I even added to my hatred because of the dreams, and I wanted to lick him out of the land of the living, as a calf licks the green grass off the ground.
So Judah and I sold him to the Ishmaelites for thirty gold pieces; we hid ten of them and showed the twenty to our brothers.
In this way I was filled with greed for his removal.
But the God of my fathers rescued him from my hands, so that I would not commit a lawless act in Israel.”
“Now hear, my children, words of truth, to do righteousness and every law of the Most High, and not to be led astray by the spirit of hatred, because it is evil in all human actions.
Whatever the one who hates does, he finds disgusting. If someone keeps the law of the Lord, he does not praise it; if someone fears the Lord and wants what is just, he does not love him;
he blames the truth, envies the one who succeeds, welcomes slander, loves arrogance; for hatred has blinded his soul, as I too saw it in the case of Joseph.”
“So guard yourselves, my children, against hatred, because it commits lawlessness against the Lord himself.
It refuses to hear the words of his commandments about love of neighbor, and it sins against God.
If a brother stumbles, it immediately wants to tell everyone and is eager to have him judged for it and punished until he dies.
If he is a slave, it sets him against his master, and in every affliction it attacks him, to see if it can put him to death.
Hatred works with envy, and it is always sick when it hears of or sees the progress of those who are doing well.

Just as love wants to give life even to the dead, and would call back those under a sentence of death, so hatred wants to kill the living, and does not want those who have sinned in some small thing to live.

The spirit of hatred, through faintheartedness, works with Satan in everything toward the death of human beings; the spirit of love, through patience, works with the law of God toward the salvation of human beings.”

“Hatred is evil, for it continually dwells with lying, speaking against the truth. It makes small things large, treats darkness as light, calls sweet things bitter, and teaches slander, war, insult, and every abundance of evil, and it fills the heart with devilish poison.
I tell you these things from experience, my children, so that you will flee hatred and cling to the love of the Lord.

Righteousness drives out hatred, and humility destroys hatred. The righteous and humble person is ashamed to do what is unjust, not because someone else condemns him but because his own heart does, for the Lord looks into his thoughts.
He does not speak against a man, since the fear of the Most High overcomes hatred.
For, afraid of offending the Lord, he does not want to wrong a person at all, not even in his thoughts.
I learned these things last, after I repented over Joseph.
True repentance before God removes disobedience, drives out darkness, lights up the eyes, gives knowledge to the soul, and guides the mind toward salvation,
and what he did not learn from human beings, he knows through repentance.
God brought a disease of the liver on me, and if it had not been for the prayers of Jacob my father, my spirit would very nearly have left me.
For a person is punished through the very things by which he breaks the law.
Since my liver had pressed mercilessly against Joseph, I suffered mercilessly in my liver, and was under judgment for eleven months, as long as I had held a grudge against Joseph, until he was sold.”
“Now, my children, each of you love your brother, and remove hatred from your hearts, loving one another in deed, in word, and in the thinking of the soul.
In front of our father I spoke peaceably to Joseph, but when I left, the spirit of hatred darkened my mind and troubled my soul to kill him.
So love one another from the heart; and if someone sins against you, tell him so in peace, driving out the poison of hatred, and keep no deceit in your soul. If he confesses and repents, forgive him;
and if he denies it, do not argue with him, in case he swears and you sin twice.

Do not let an outsider hear your secret in a quarrel, so that he does not come to hate you and become your enemy and commit a great sin against you; for often he speaks deceitfully, or schemes against you for evil, having taken poison from you.

If he denies it, but is ashamed when he is reproved, let it rest; do not drag him out. The one who denies it is repenting, so that he will not offend you again; he will even honor you, fear you, and be at peace with you.
But if he is shameless and persists in evil, even so forgive him from your heart, and give vengeance to God.”
“If anyone prospers more than you, do not be sad; rather pray for him, that he may prosper completely. Perhaps it is good for you this way.
If he is lifted up still more, do not envy him, remembering that all flesh will die. Offer a hymn to the Lord, who provides good and helpful things to all people.
Examine the Lord’s judgments, and so you will let it go, and your mind will be quiet.
If someone does get rich from evil, like Esau, my father’s brother, do not be jealous; wait for the Lord’s limit.
For either he takes those things away from him in misfortune, or he forgives the repentant, or he keeps punishment forever for the unrepentant.
The poor person who has plenty, giving thanks to the Lord in all things, is rich in every way, because he does not have the evil distraction of people.
So remove hatred from your souls, and love one another with uprightness of heart.”
“Tell these things also to your children, so that they will honor Judah and Levi, for from them the Lord will raise up a savior for Israel.
I know that in the end your children will fall away from them, and will be before the Lord in all wickedness, ill-treatment, and corruption.”
After resting a little, he said to them again, “My children, obey your father, and bury me near my fathers.”
He stretched out his feet and fell asleep in peace.
Five years later they carried him up and laid him in Hebron with his fathers.

notes.text: “Gad” (Hebrew *Gad*) means “good fortune” (Gen 30:11).
“Two stadia.” A stadion was about 607 feet (185 m), so two stadia is about 1,200 feet, or about 0.23 mile (370 m).

chapters.heading: The Testament of Gad, on Hatred

verses.text: A copy of the testament of Asher,{a} what he said to his sons in the hundred and twentieth year of his life.
While he was still in good health, he said to them, “Listen, children of Asher, to your father, and I will show you everything that is right before God.
God has given the sons of men two ways, two inclinations, two kinds of action, two places, and two ends.
So all things are two, one set against the other.
There are two ways, of good and of evil; and in our chests are the two inclinations that distinguish between them.
If the soul wants to go the good way, every action of it is in righteousness, and if it sins, it repents at once.
For by thinking just thoughts and throwing away wickedness, it immediately overturns evil and uproots sin.

But if the inclination leans toward evil, every action of it is in wickedness; it pushes good away and takes evil in; it is ruled by Beliar, and even if it does something good, it twists it into wickedness.
When it begins as if doing good, the end of its action drives it to do evil, because the treasury of the devil is full of the poison of an evil spirit.”
“There is a soul, he says, that speaks the good in place of the evil, and yet leads the end of the matter into badness.
There is a person who has no pity on someone who serves him in evil; this too is two-faced, but the whole is evil.
There is a person who loves the one who does evil; he too is in wickedness, since he chooses even to die in evil for him. It is clear that this too is two-faced, but the whole is a bad action.
Even where there is love, it is wickedness if it hides the evil; it is good in name, as it were, but the end of the action comes to evil.
Another steals, wrongs, robs, and is greedy, and yet has mercy on the poor; this too is two-faced, but the whole is evil.

Someone who cheats his neighbor angers God, perjures himself against the Most High, and yet has mercy on the poor; he rejects and provokes the Lord who gave the commandment of the law, and gives rest to the needy;
he stains the soul and makes the body shine; he kills many and shows mercy to few. This too is two-faced.

Another commits adultery and sexual immorality, and stays away from rich foods; when he fasts, he does evil; with power and wealth he sweeps many away, and out of his swollen wickedness he keeps commandments. This too is two-faced, but the whole is evil.
People like this are like swine and hares, because they are half clean, but in truth they are unclean.
For so God has said, on the tablets of heaven.”
“So you, my children, do not be two-faced like them, partly good and partly bad; hold only to goodness, because God rests in it, and people long for it;
run away from wickedness, destroying the devil by your good actions. For the two-faced do not serve God but their own desires, in order to please Beliar and people like themselves.”
“Good people who are single-faced, even if they are thought by the two-faced to sin, are righteous before God.
Many who kill the wicked do two works, an evil through a good, but the whole is good, because by uprooting the evil he has destroyed it.

There is someone who hates the merciful person and wrongs the adulterer and the robber; this too looks two-faced, but the whole work is good, because he imitates the Lord by not accepting what seems good together with real evil.
Another does not want to see a good day with the wasteful, so that he does not defile his mouth and pollute his soul. This too looks two-faced, but the whole is good,

because such people are like roe deer and deer: in a wild way of life they seem unclean, but they are entirely clean, because they walk in zeal for God, staying away from what God also hates and forbids by his commands, keeping evil away from the good.”
“See, then, children, how there are two in everything, one set against the other, and one hidden by the other.
Death follows life, dishonor follows glory, night follows day, and darkness follows light; but all things are under the day, and just things under life; therefore eternal life also awaits death.
It is not possible to call truth a lie, or the just unjust; for all truth is under the light, as all things are under God.

I have tested all this in my life, and I have not strayed from the truth of the Lord, and I have sought out the commands of the Most High, walking with all my strength single-facedly toward the good.”
“So you too, children, pay attention to the commands of the Lord, following the truth single-facedly,
for the two-faced are punished twice. Hate the spirits of error that fight against a person.
Keep the law of the Lord, and do not treat evil as good; look instead to what is truly good, and keep it in all the Lord’s commands, turning to him and finding rest in him,
because the ends of people show their righteousness, and make known the angels of the Lord and of Satan.
If the soul leaves in turmoil, it is tormented by the evil spirit it served in desires and evil deeds;
but if it leaves quietly, in joy, it has known the angel of peace, and he will comfort it in life.”
“Do not be, children, like Sodom, which did not recognize the angels of the Lord and was destroyed forever.

I know that you will sin and be handed over into the hands of your enemies; your land will be laid waste, and you will be scattered to the four corners of the earth, and in the dispersion you will be despised like worthless water,

until the Most High visits the earth; coming himself as a man, eating and drinking with people, and quietly crushing the head of the dragon through water. He will save Israel and all the nations, God disguised as a man.
So tell your children these things, so that they will not disobey him.
For I read on the tablets of heaven that you will certainly disobey him and certainly act ungodly toward him, not paying attention to the law of God but to the commands of people.
For this reason you will be scattered, like Gad and Dan my brothers, who will not know their land, tribe, or language.
But the Lord will gather you in faith, through the hope of his compassion, for the sake of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.”
After telling them these things, he commanded them, saying, “Bury me in Hebron.” And he died, falling asleep in a good sleep;
and after this his sons did as he had commanded them, and carried him up and buried him with his fathers.

notes.text: “Asher” (Hebrew *Asher*) means “happy” or “fortunate” (Gen 30:13).

chapters.heading: The Testament of Asher, on the Two Faces of Vice and Virtue

verses.text: A copy of the testament of Joseph.{a} When he was about to die, he called his sons and his brothers and said to them,
“My children and brothers, listen to Joseph, beloved of Israel; give ear, sons, to your father.
In my life I have seen envy and death, and I did not stray from the truth of the Lord.
These brothers of mine hated me, and the Lord loved me; they wanted to kill me, and the God of my fathers kept me safe; they lowered me into a pit, and the Most High brought me up;
I was sold as a slave, and the Lord freed me; I was taken into captivity, and his strong hand helped me; I was held in hunger, and the Lord himself fed me;
I was alone, and God comforted me; I was sick, and the Most High visited me; I was in prison, and the Savior showed me favor; I was in chains, and he released me;
I was under slander, and he pleaded my case; I was under the bitter words of the Egyptians, and he rescued me; I was among envies and deceits, and he lifted me up.”
“So Photimar, the chief cook of Pharaoh, entrusted his house to me.
I struggled against a shameless woman who pressed me to break the law with her; but the God of Israel my father kept me from a blazing flame.
I was imprisoned, beaten, and mocked; and the Lord gave me pity in the eyes of the prison keeper.
For he will never abandon those who fear him, not in darkness, nor in chains, nor in afflictions, nor in hardships.
God is not ashamed like a human being, he does not shrink back like a son of man, he does not grow weak or give up like one born of the earth;
he stands by in every place, and he comforts in different ways, withdrawing for a short time in order to test the purpose of the soul.
He showed me to be approved in ten trials, and in all of them I was patient; for patience is a great medicine, and endurance gives many good things.”
“How often did the Egyptian woman threaten me with death! How often, after handing me over to punishment, did she call me back and threaten me when I would not go to bed with her! And she said to me,
‘You will rule over me and over everything I have, if you give yourself to me, and you will be our master.’
So I remembered the words of the fathers of my father Jacob, and going into my room, I prayed to the Lord,
and I fasted during those seven years, and I looked to the Egyptian woman as if I were living in luxury; for those who fast for God gain a gracious face.
If she gave me wine, I did not drink; and going without food for three days at a time, I took my meal and gave it to the poor and the sick.
I rose early to pray to the Lord, and I wept over Memphia the Egyptian, because she pestered me so constantly; at night she would come to me on the pretext of a visit.
At first, because she had no male child, she pretended to take me as her son. I prayed to the Lord, and she bore a male child.
For some time she embraced me as a son, and I did not realize; but in the end she was drawing me into sexual immorality.
When I understood, I was grieved to the point of death. When she left, I came to myself, and I mourned over her for many days, because I knew her deceit and her error.
I spoke to her the words of the Most High, in case she would turn away from her wicked desire.”
“How often did she flatter me with words, as if I were a holy man, deceitfully praising my self-control in front of her husband, but wanting to trip me alone!

She praised me openly as self-controlled, and secretly said to me, ‘Do not be afraid of my husband; he is convinced about your self-control, and even if someone tells him about us, he will not believe it.’
Through all this I lay on the ground in sackcloth and begged God that the Lord would rescue me from the Egyptian woman.
When she accomplished nothing, she came to me again on the pretext of instruction, to learn the word of the Lord.
She said to me, ‘If you want me to leave my idols, be persuaded by me; and I will persuade the Egyptian to give up his idols, so that we may walk in the law of your Lord.’
I said to her, ‘The Lord does not say that those who revere him are in uncleanness, and he takes no pleasure in adulterers.’
She fell silent, longing to carry out her desire.
I added fasting and prayer, so that the Lord would rescue me from her.”
“At another time she said to me, ‘If you do not want to commit adultery, I will kill the Egyptian, and then I will take you lawfully as my husband.’
When I heard this, I tore my robe and said, ‘Woman, respect the Lord and do not do this wicked deed, or you will be destroyed; I will even tell everyone about your plan of ungodliness.’
Frightened, she begged me not to tell anyone of her wickedness.
And she went away, trying to warm me with gifts, and sending me every pleasure of the sons of men.”
“She sent me food mixed with sorcery.
When the eunuch who brought it came, I looked up and saw a fearsome man handing me a sword along with the dish. I understood that her scheme was meant to lead my soul astray.
When he left, I wept, and tasted neither that food nor any of her dainties.
After a day she came to me, recognized the food, and said to me, ‘Why is it that you did not eat any of the food?’
I said to her, ‘Because you filled it with death. How could you say that you do not approach idols, but only the Lord?
Now know that the God of my father revealed your wickedness to me through an angel, and I kept the food to show you your guilt, in case you would see it and repent.

So that you may learn that the wickedness of the ungodly does not overpower those who worship God in self-control, I took it in front of her and ate, saying, “The God of my fathers and the angel of Abraham will be with me.”’
She fell on her face at my feet and wept. I raised her up and warned her,
and she promised not to do this ungodly act again.”
“But since her heart was set on me for indulgence, she kept falling at my feet, groaning.

When the Egyptian husband saw her, he said to her, ‘Why has your face fallen?’ She said, ‘I have a pain in my heart, and the groans of my spirit are holding me.’ And he tended her though she was not ill.
Then she jumped at me while her husband was still outside, and said to me, ‘I will hang myself, or throw myself into a well or off a cliff, unless you are persuaded by me.’
Understanding that the spirit of Beliar was troubling her, I prayed to the Lord and said to her,

‘Why are you troubled and in an uproar, blinded by your sins? Remember that if you kill yourself, Sethon, your husband’s concubine and your rival, will beat your children and wipe out your memory from the earth.’
She said to me, ‘See, then, you love me. It is enough for me that you care about my life and my children’s. I expect to enjoy my desire.’
She did not know that I spoke this way because of my God, and not because of her.

For if someone falls under the passion of an evil desire and is enslaved to it, as she was, even if he hears something good, he takes it as it applies to the passion that has beaten him, toward evil desire.”

“I tell you, children, it was about noon{b} when she left me; and I knelt before the Lord the whole day and into the whole night, and toward dawn I rose in tears, asking for rescue from the Egyptian woman.
In the end she took hold of my clothes and dragged me by force to lie with her.
When I saw that in her frenzy she held my clothes by force, I fled naked.
She slandered me to her husband; and the Egyptian put me in prison in his house, and the next day he flogged me and sent me to the prison in his house.

While I was in chains, the Egyptian woman became ill from grief, and listened to me singing to the Lord in the house of darkness, rejoicing in a glad voice and glorifying my God, only because I had a reason to be free of the Egyptian woman.”
“She often sent to me, saying, ‘Agree to fulfill my desire, and I will free you from your chains and take you out of the darkness.’
I never bent toward her even in thought. For God loves the one who fasts in self-control in a pit of darkness more than the one who lives in luxury in the inner rooms with indulgence.
The one who lives in self-control also wants glory, and if the Most High knows it is good for him, he provides this too, as he did for me.
How often, though she was ill, did she come down to me at an untimely hour and hear my voice praying! When I understood her groans, I kept silent.

When I was in her house, she would uncover her arms, chest, and legs, so that I would fall for her; for she was very beautiful, especially when dressed up to trick me. But the Lord kept me from her attempts.”
“See, then, my children, how much patience accomplishes, and prayer with fasting.
You too, if you pursue self-control and purity with patience and humility of heart, the Lord will live in you, because he loves self-control.

Where the Most High lives, even if someone falls into envy, slavery, or slander, the Lord who lives in him, because of his self-control, not only rescues him from evil, but also lifts him up and glorifies him, as he did me.
Every person is held in some way, either in deed, in word, or in thought.
My brothers know how my father loved me; and I was not lifted up in my heart. Although I was a child, I had the fear of God in my mind, for I knew that everything will pass away,

and I measured myself and honored my brothers. Out of respect for them I kept silent while being sold, and did not tell the Ishmaelites my family, that I am the son of Jacob, a great and powerful man.”
“You too, then, have the fear of God in your actions and honor your brothers. Everyone who keeps the law of the Lord will be loved by him.
When I came to the Indocolpites with the Ishmaelites, they asked me; and I said that I was their slave, born in their house, so that I would not shame my brothers.
The eldest of them said to me, ‘You are not a slave, for your face shows what you are’; and he threatened me with death. But I kept saying that I was their slave.
When we came to Egypt, they fought over me, over who would give gold to get me.
So everyone decided that I would stay in Egypt with a trader of theirs until they came back bringing merchandise.
The Lord gave me favor in the eyes of the trader, and he entrusted his house to me.
The Lord blessed him by my hand, and made him rich in silver and gold;
and I was with him three months and five days.”
“At that time Memphia, the wife of Potiphar,{c} came by with great splendor, and set her eyes on me, because the eunuchs had told her about me.
She told her husband about the trader, that he had grown rich through a young Hebrew; and she said, ‘They say they stole him by theft from the land of Canaan.
Now hold a trial with him, and take the young man for your steward; and the God of the Hebrews will bless you, because heavenly grace is on him.’”
“Potiphar, persuaded by her words, ordered the trader to be brought and said to him, ‘What is this I hear, that you are stealing people from the land of the Hebrews and selling them as slaves?’
The trader fell on his face and begged, saying, ‘I beg you, my lord, I do not know what you are saying.’
He said, ‘Then where did you get the Hebrew boy?’ He answered, ‘The Ishmaelites left him with me until they come back.’
He did not believe him, but ordered him to be beaten naked. When he held to his story, Potiphar said, ‘Bring the young man.’
I was brought in and bowed to the chief eunuch; for he was third in rank under Pharaoh, a ruler over all the eunuchs, with a wife, children, and concubines.
He separated me from the trader and said to me, ‘Are you a slave or free?’ I said, ‘A slave.’
He said to me, ‘Whose slave?’ I said, ‘The Ishmaelites’.’
Again he said to me, ‘How did you become their slave?’ I said that they had bought me in Canaan.
He did not believe it, saying, ‘You are lying’; and he ordered me beaten naked.”
“Memphia saw through a window that I was being beaten, and sent word to her husband, saying, ‘Your judgment is unjust, because you punish a free person who was stolen, as if he had done wrong.’
When I did not change my story under the beating, he ordered me imprisoned, until, he said, the boy’s owners came.
His wife said to him, ‘Why do you hold the captive, a boy of noble birth, who ought rather to be free and to serve you?’
She wanted to see me in longing for sin; and in all this I did not realize it.
He said to Memphia, ‘Among the Egyptians it is not the custom to take away another’s property before there is proof.’
He said this about the trader, and about me, that I should be locked up.”
“After twenty-four days the Ishmaelites came; and having heard that Jacob my father was mourning over me, they said to me,
‘Why did you say you were a slave? We have found that you are the son of a great man in Canaan, and your father is mourning for you in a pit.’
I wanted to weep again, but held myself back so that I would not shame my brothers. And I said, ‘I do not know; I am a slave.’
Then they planned to sell me, so that I would not be found in their hands.
They were afraid of Jacob, that he would take revenge on them with danger; for it was said that he is great with the Lord and with people.
Then the trader said to them, ‘Free me from the judgment of Potiphar.’
They came and asked me for it, saying, ‘He was bought by us with silver, and he let us go.’”
“Memphia told her husband to buy me, saying, ‘I hear they are selling him.’
He sent a eunuch to the Ishmaelites, asking to buy me;
and when they did not want to deal with him, he withdrew. The eunuch, having tried them, told his mistress that they were asking a high price for the boy.
She sent another eunuch, saying, ‘Even if they ask for two and a half pounds{d} of gold, take care not to spare the gold; just buy the boy and bring him.’
She gave them eighty gold pieces for me, and told the Egyptian woman’s husband that a hundred had been given for me.
When I saw this, I kept silent, so that the eunuch would not be questioned.”
“See, children, how much I endured so as not to shame my brothers.
You too, love one another, and in patience cover over one another’s faults.
For God is pleased with harmony among brothers, and with a choice of heart that is content with love.
When my brothers came into Egypt and learned that I had returned their silver to them, and I did not reproach them but comforted them,
and after Jacob’s death I loved them even more, and I did everything he commanded and more, and they were amazed.
I did not let them be distressed over even a small thing; whatever was in my hand, I gave to them.
Their sons were my sons, and my sons were like their servants; their soul was my soul, every pain of theirs my pain, and every sickness of theirs my sickness; my land was theirs, my counsel theirs.
I did not exalt myself over them in boasting because of my worldly glory, but was among them as one of the least.”
“So if you too walk in the commands of the Lord, my children, he will lift you up here, and will bless you with good things forever.
If anyone wants to do you evil, do good and pray for him; and you will be rescued from every evil through the Lord.
See that because of my patience I even took a daughter of my lords as a wife, and 7,500 pounds of gold{e} were given to me with her; for the Lord made them serve me.
He gave me beauty, like a flower above the beautiful ones of Israel; and he kept me to old age in strength and beauty, for I was like Jacob in everything.”
“Listen, my children, to the dreams I saw.
Twelve deer were grazing, and nine of them were divided and scattered over the earth; likewise the three.

I saw that from Judah was born a virgin, wearing a linen robe; and from her came a spotless lamb, and on his left something like a lion; and all the wild animals rushed against him, and the lamb overcame them and destroyed them, to be trampled.
The angels rejoiced over him, and the people, and all the earth.
These things will happen in their time, in the last days.
So you, my children, keep the commands of the Lord, and honor Judah and Levi; for from them the Lamb of God will rise for you, saving all the nations and Israel by grace.
For his kingdom is an everlasting kingdom that will not be shaken; but my kingdom among you will come to an end, like a fruit-watchman’s hut, which is not seen after summer.”
“I know that after my death the Egyptians will oppress you; but God will take vengeance for you and bring you into the promise of your fathers.
But you must carry my bones up with you, for when my bones are taken up, the Lord will be with you in light, and Beliar will be in darkness with the Egyptians.
Take your mother Zilpah too, and lay her near Bilhah, by the Hippodrome, close to Rachel.”
After saying this, he stretched out his feet and fell asleep with the sleep of eternity.
All Israel mourned him, and all of Egypt with a great mourning.
For he had shared the suffering of the Egyptians as if they were his own limbs, and had done them good, standing with them in every work, plan, and matter.

notes.text: “Joseph” (Hebrew *Yosef*) means “may he add,” from Gen 30:24, “May Yahweh add to me another son.”
The Greek says “about the sixth hour,” counted from sunrise, which is about noon.
“Potiphar” (Hebrew *Potifar*) is from an Egyptian name meaning “the one whom Ra gave.” The Greek spells it “Petephri” or “Petephris.”
“Two minas.” A mina was one-sixtieth of a talent, about 1.25 pounds (0.57 kg), so two minas is about 2.5 pounds (1.1 kg) of gold.
“A hundred talents.” A talent was about 75 pounds (34 kg), so a hundred talents is about 7,500 pounds (3,400 kg).

chapters.heading: The Testament of Joseph, on Self-Control

verses.text: A copy of the words of Benjamin,{a} which he laid down for his sons, having lived a hundred and twenty years.
He kissed them and said, “As Isaac was born to Abraham in his hundredth year, so I was to Jacob.
Since Rachel died giving birth to me, I had no milk, and so I was nursed by her maid Bilhah.
For after bearing Joseph Rachel was barren for twelve years; she prayed to the Lord with fasting for twelve days; and then she conceived and bore me.
Our father loved Rachel very much, and prayed to see two sons from her.
For this reason I was called ‘son of days,’ which is Benjamin.”
“When I came into Egypt and my brother Joseph recognized me, he said to me, ‘What did you tell my father when they sold me?’
I told him they had smeared your tunic with blood and sent it, saying, ‘See whether this is your son’s tunic.’
He said to me, ‘Yes, brother; for when the Ishmaelites took me, one of them stripped off my tunic, gave me a loincloth, flogged me, and told me to run.
As he went off to hide my cloak, a lion met him and killed him.
So his companions were frightened and sold me on to others.’”
“So you too, my children, love the Lord, the God of heaven, and keep his commands, imitating the good and holy man Joseph.
Let your mind be set on the good, as you know I have been. Whoever has a good mind sees everything rightly.

Fear the Lord and love your neighbor; and if the spirits of Beliar demand you for every kind of affliction, no wickedness of affliction will overpower you, just as it did not overpower my brother Joseph.
How many people wanted to kill him, and God protected him! For the one who fears God and loves his neighbor cannot be struck by the airy spirit of Beliar, being covered by the fear of God;
and he cannot be overpowered by the plots of people or of wild animals, being helped by the Lord’s love, which he has for his neighbor.
I begged our father Jacob to pray for our brothers, that the Lord would not count against them whatever evil they had thought against him.
Jacob cried out, ‘O my child Joseph, you have overcome the heart of Jacob your father.’ He embraced him, and for two hours kissed him, saying,

‘The prophecy of heaven about the Lamb of God and Savior of the world will be fulfilled in you: that a spotless one will be handed over for the lawless, and a sinless one will die for the ungodly, in the blood of a covenant, for the salvation of the nations and of Israel, and he will destroy Beliar and those who serve him.’”
“Have you seen, children, the end of the good man? Imitate his compassion with a good mind, so that you too may wear crowns of glory.
The good man does not have a dark eye; for he has mercy on all, even if they are sinners,
even if they plot evil against him. So the one who does good overcomes evil, covered by the good; and he loves the righteous as his own soul.

If someone is honored, he is not envious; if someone is rich, he is not jealous; if someone is brave, he praises him; he trusts and sings the praise of the self-controlled; he has mercy on the poor; he sympathizes with the weak; he sings praise to God;

he defends the one who has the fear of God; he works with the one who loves God; the one who rejects the Most High he warns and turns back, and the one who has the grace of a good spirit he loves as his own soul.”

“If you have a good mind, children, even evil people will be at peace with you, the wasteful will respect you and turn to good, and the greedy will not only give up their passion but will even give what they got by greed to the afflicted.
If you keep doing good, even the unclean spirits will flee from you, and the wild animals themselves will flee from you in fear.
For where there is the fear of good works in the mind, darkness runs away from it.
If someone insults a holy man, he repents; for the holy man has mercy on the abuser, and is silent.
And if someone betrays a righteous soul, and the righteous one prays and is humbled for a little while, he afterward appears much brighter, as my brother Joseph did.”
“The plan of the good man is not in the hand of the spirit of error, Beliar; for the angel of peace guides his soul.
He does not look with passion at perishable things, or gather wealth for the love of pleasure.
He does not delight in pleasure, does not hurt his neighbor, is not stuffed with food, and is not led astray by raising his eyes; for the Lord is his portion.

The good mind does not accept the glory and dishonor of human beings, and knows no deceit or lie, no fighting or abuse. For the Lord lives in it, lights up its soul, and it rejoices toward everyone at all times.

The good mind does not have two tongues, of blessing and cursing, of insult and honor, of sadness and joy, of quiet and disturbance, of hypocrisy and truth, of poverty and wealth; it has one single pure and sincere attitude toward everyone.
It has no double sight or hearing; for in everything it does, says, or sees, it knows that the Lord is watching over its soul,
and cleansing its mind, so that it will not be condemned by God or people. Every work of Beliar is double, and has no simplicity.”
“So, my children, flee the wickedness of Beliar, because he gives a sword to those who obey him.

The sword is the mother of seven evils. First the mind conceives through Beliar; the first is envy; the second, destruction; the third, affliction; the fourth, captivity; the fifth, want; the sixth, disorder; the seventh, desolation.
For this reason Cain was also handed over by God to seven punishments; for every hundred years the Lord brought one blow on him.

He suffered for two hundred years, and in the nine hundredth year he was made desolate, at the flood, because of Abel his righteous brother. In his seven hundred years Cain was judged, and Lamech in seventy times seven;
for forever, those who become like Cain in envy, to the point of hating their brothers, will be judged by the same punishment.”
“So you too, my children, run away from wickedness, envy, and hatred of brothers, and cling to goodness and love.
The one who has a pure mind in love does not look at a woman for sexual immorality; for he has no pollution in his heart, because the Spirit of God rests in him.

Just as the sun is not polluted by shining on dung and mud, but instead dries both and drives away the stench, so the pure mind, held among the pollutions of the earth, rather builds up, and is not itself polluted.”

“I suspect that there will be actions among you that are not good, from the words of Enoch the righteous. You will commit the sexual immorality of Sodom, and be destroyed, all but a few, and renew wantonness with women; and the kingdom of the Lord will not be among you, for he will take it away at once.

Yet in your portion the temple of God will be built, and it will be glorious among you. For he will take it, and the twelve tribes will be gathered there, and all the nations, until the Most High sends his salvation, in the visitation of an only-begotten one.
He will go into the first temple, and there the Lord will be insulted and despised, and lifted up on a tree.
The curtain of the temple will be torn, and the Spirit of God will pass on to the nations, like fire poured out.
Having come up out of Hades, he will go up from earth to heaven. I know how humble he will be on earth, and how glorious in heaven.”
“When Joseph was in Egypt, I longed to see his appearance and the shape of his face; and through the prayers of Jacob my father I saw him, awake, in the daytime, just as his whole appearance was.
Know, then, my children, that I am dying.
So practice truth and righteousness, each with his neighbor, and justice for confirmation, and keep the law of the Lord and his commands;
for these things I teach you in place of every inheritance. So give them to your children, too, as an everlasting possession. For Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob did this.
All these things they left us as an inheritance, saying, ‘Keep the commands of God, until the Lord reveals his salvation to all the nations.’
Then you will see Enoch, Noah, Shem, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob rising on the right hand, in joy.
Then we too will rise, each at our scepter, worshiping the King of heaven, who appeared on earth in the form of a man of humility. All who believed in him on earth will rejoice with him.
Then everyone will rise, some to glory and some to dishonor. The Lord will judge Israel first for its wrong against him, because they did not believe in God who came in flesh as deliverer.
Then he will judge all the nations, as many as did not believe in him when he appeared on earth;

and he will convict Israel among the chosen of the nations, as he convicted Esau among the Midianites, who deceived their brothers into sexual immorality and idolatry; they were estranged from God, becoming not children in the portion of those who fear the Lord.
But if you walk in holiness in the sight of the Lord, you will again live in hope in me; and all Israel will be gathered to the Lord.”
“No longer will I be called a ravening wolf because of your plundering, but a worker of the Lord, handing out food to those who do good.

In later times there will rise from my seed one beloved of the Lord, hearing his voice on earth, enlightening all the nations with new knowledge, a light of knowledge stepping into Israel for salvation; he will snatch from it like a wolf and give to the assembly of the nations.
Until the end of the ages he will be in the assemblies of the nations and among their rulers, like a musical tune in the mouth of all;
and he will be written about in holy books, both his work and his word; and he will be God’s chosen one forever;
and because of him Jacob my father instructed me, saying, ‘He will fill up what is lacking in your tribe.’”
When he had finished his words, he said, “I command you, my children, to carry my bones up from Egypt and bury me in Hebron, near my fathers.”
Benjamin died at the age of a hundred and twenty-five, in a good old age; and they placed him in a coffin.

In the ninety-first year after the Exodus of the sons of Israel from Egypt, they and their brothers carried up the bones of their fathers secretly, to the place called Canaan; and they buried them in Hebron, at the feet of their fathers.
Then they returned from the land of Canaan and lived in Egypt until the day of their departure from the land of Egypt.

notes.text: “Benjamin” (Hebrew *Binyamin*) is usually explained as “son of the right hand” or “son of the south” (Gen 35:18). This book explains it as “son of days” (1.6).
